chunks.heading: Agent Management
chunks.text: Guide for creating, configuring, and utilizing agents

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text: Agents go beyond simple chat functionality to serve as business-specific AI interfaces that connect various tools and knowledge within an organization. Users input requests in natural language, and agents provide automated responses based on defined purposes and tools.

chunks.heading: Concept Definition
chunks.text:
Agents are composed of the following elements:
Instruction (Action Guidelines): Defines what roles and actions the LLM should perform
LLM Model: Selects AI models like GPT-5, Claude to provide the intelligence foundation for agents
MCP Tool (Interface with External Systems): Integrates with external systems like GitHub, Notion, Snowflake
Knowledge Bundle (Vector-based Organizational Knowledge): Vectorizes organizational documents and data to utilize as searchable knowledge
This combination is configured in the admin interface, and users can utilize agents shared within the organization.

chunks.heading: Agent Components and Operating Principles
chunks.text:
Agents are defined by the following components.
Component | Description
LLM Model | Select from pre-registered models like GPT-5, Claude (future support for custom API keys, BYOK)
Instruction | Role definition at prompt level. Specifies what responses to elicit from LLM
MCP Tool | Tools for controlling external systems like GitHub, Notion, Snowflake
Knowledge Bundle | Search sources with embedded data collected from files, GitHub, Drive, etc.

chunks.heading: Agent Types
chunks.text:
Agents are classified into two types:
Built-in: Agents that can be installed through the agent library and used immediately. You can use default agents or pre-configure agents needed by your organization.
Custom: Agents that organizational administrators can create by directly configuring agent components.

chunks.heading: Agent Status
chunks.text:
The main statuses used in Agent Management are as follows:
Enabled: Status where configuration is completed normally and the agent can be shared and executed by users. Agents cannot be modified or deleted while in Enabled status.
Disabled: Temporarily deactivated status where the agent is not exposed to users.

chunks.heading: Agent Publication Approval Workflow
chunks.text:
When the approval workflow is enabled, an administrator or owner can review an organization agent’s settings and purpose before an AI operator publishes it to users. The approval target is the action of changing a Disabled organization agent to Enabled.
The AI operator configures the agent and requests publication approval. Administrators and owners review the requested agent’s settings, share scope, and request reason, then decide whether to publish it.
How an AI operator requests publication approval
In Agent Management, try to activate the agent you want to publish.
Check the share scope. If you need to change the target audience, click Edit Share Scope and update the share scope.
Click Request Approval and enter the request reason.
When the request is created, you are moved to the approval request detail page and the status is shown as Pending.
While a request is pending, the agent’s share settings and status cannot be changed. The requester can open the approval request detail page to check the request and review status, or cancel the request before it is reviewed.
How an administrator or owner reviews an approval request
In Agent Management, go to Approval Workflow.
Filter the request list by request status, or search by agent name or requester.
On the approval request detail page, review the request reason, agent information, current status, and review history.
If needed, click Go to Agent Test to check the settings and test chat results.
If the agent can be published, click Approve and Publish and enter the review reason.

chunks.heading: Agent Publication Approval Workflow
chunks.text:
If changes are needed, click Reject and enter the rejection reason.
When approved, the agent changes to Enabled and is published to users according to the configured share scope. When rejected, the agent is not published, and the AI operator can update the agent settings and request approval again.
Approval workflow settings
Administrators and owners can turn this feature on or off at the top of the approval workflow page.
When the feature is off: turn on the Approval Workflow switch shown at the top right of the page.
When the feature is on: click the settings icon next to the page title, then turn off the Approval Workflow switch in the popover.
If the workflow is turned off, AI operators can publish agents without administrator or owner review. If there are pending requests, you can select Cancel pending requests together in the confirmation dialog to cancel the remaining approval requests at the same time.
When an administrator or owner activates an agent directly, it can be published without a separate approval request.

chunks.heading: Custom Agent Creation
chunks.text:
Click the “Create Agent” button to input agent name and summary information, then create a Custom agent.
Administrators can configure the following items in the agent detail screen:
Agent Name: Set a unique name for the agent. It’s recommended to use a clear name that’s easy to identify within the organization.
Summary: A short description summarizing the agent’s functionality in one line. Users can refer to this when selecting agents.
Icon: Upload an icon to visually distinguish the agent, or click Generate icon to create an icon that matches the Agent Name and Summary. Credits are used when generating icons, and generated icons can be regenerated if needed.
Description: Detailed description of the agent to be displayed to users. Clearly explains the tasks the agent can perform and its main features.
Prompt Guide: Example questions to guide users. Up to 5 can be registered, showing users how to utilize the agent.
LLM Model: Select the AI model the agent will use. Supports latest high-performance models such as Claude Opus 4.7, OpenAI GPT-5.5, and Google Gemini 3.5 Flash.
Wide Context: (Supported models only) Expands the context window up to 1M tokens to process long documents or large amounts of data. Can be enabled in Claude 4.5 Sonnet, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 Mini, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, and Gemini 3.5 Flash models.
Thinking Mode (Supported models only): Supports Adaptive Thinking and Extended Thinking modes, providing more in-depth analysis for complex reasoning tasks.

chunks.heading: Custom Agent Creation
chunks.text:
Instruction: Define the agent’s role and action guidelines. Specifies how the LLM should respond, what tone and style to maintain, etc. When writing an Instruction, clicking the Enhance Instruction text button displayed at the top of the input field allows you to automatically generate a detailed Instruction from a simple phrase (at least 10 characters).
MCP Tool Addition: Add tools that can integrate with external systems. Can connect with various services like GitHub, Notion, databases. OAuth integration is supported even in Custom MCPs used by agents, and it is compatible with OAuth MCPs regardless of DCR (Dynamic Client Registration) support.
Edge Tunnel Settings: When connecting tools in a private network or local environment, you can use Edge Tunnel for secure integration.
Personal Edge Tunnel: Connect via a tunnel running on a personal PC.
Org Edge Tunnel (Enterprise Plan only): Connect via an organization-managed tunnel, allowing team members to use tools without running separate tunnels.
Add Skill: Connect public skills registered by the administrator to the agent. Selecting a skill uploaded in Skill Management allows the agent to utilize that skill as needed during conversation.
Edge Tunnel Scope: If a Skill needs to access a local network or internal system, configure Edge Tunnel Scope under the Skill. Depending on the scope, Sandbox tasks can access internal resources through the user’s Personal Edge Tunnel or an Org Edge Tunnel.

chunks.heading: Custom Agent Creation
chunks.text:
Knowledge Bundle: Connect knowledge sources that the agent can reference. Can utilize organizational documents, databases, files as vectorized searchable knowledge.
Allow File Upload: When enabled, the file upload feature (text, images) will be displayed on the user’s agent chat screen. Users can select files from local devices or My Drive to perform tasks.
Use Web apps, Widgets, and TTS: Depending on the enabled features and connected tools, the agent can create Web apps, create widgets, and provide spoken responses.
Suppress Personal Memory: When enabled, the agent will not save or use users’ personal memory in future conversations. When this option is enabled by the administrator, users cannot change their personal memory settings.
DLP Settings: Apply DLP (Data Loss Prevention) policies to agent chat to prevent sensitive information leakage from both user inputs and AI responses.
Use Organization Settings: Applies the policy configured in Security > DLP Management as-is.
Custom: Define a DLP policy individually for the agent. Refer to the DLP Management menu for detailed configuration.
External Service Connection: Allows external services that support the A2A protocol to call this agent. The organization’s external service connection policy must be enabled first.
Test Chat: Immediately test the agent’s behavior via text chat on the right side of the screen (Note: File uploads and the Artifact feature are unavailable).
MCP Tools can be added in two ways:
Select default MCP servers and tools
Direct registration of Custom Remote MCP
Authentication Method

chunks.heading: Custom Agent Creation
chunks.text:
You can select authentication methods when adding MCP Tools to agents.
Admin Authentication Delegation (Use with admin-provided credentials): Method where administrators complete authentication in advance and delegate it to users. Current default value.
User Authentication Required (Require User Authentication): Method that provides users with direct MCP server configuration and authentication when using agents. (Custom Remote MCP also supports OAuth authentication.)

chunks.heading: Agent Detail Page
chunks.text:
The agent detail page provides different management features depending on Custom Agent and Built-in Agent.
Custom Agent
An agent created directly by administrators with complete freedom to modify all components.
Full Edit Permissions: Can modify all settings including agent name, description, Prompt Guide, Icon, LLM model, Instruction
Tool and Knowledge Management: Free configuration including MCP Tool addition/deletion, Knowledge Bundle connection/disconnection
Advanced Settings: Can adjust detailed options like Artifact activation, Max Token settings
Immediate Save: Changes are reflected immediately, allowing real-time agent behavior verification
Built-in Agent
An agent installed from the agent library with limited edit permissions.
Limited Edit Permissions: Only agent name can be modified, core settings cannot be changed
Tool Integration Only: Only MCP Tool authentication and integration settings can be added
Fixed Configuration: LLM model, Instruction, Knowledge Bundle, etc. maintain pre-defined states
Stability Priority: Core setting changes are restricted to maintain original agent stability

chunks.heading: External Service Connection Settings
chunks.text:
External service connection lets external services that support the A2A protocol call an organization agent directly. For example, a user can call an agent from an external work tool, send a question, and let the agent respond using its configured Instruction, Skill, Integration, and Knowledge.
Before you start
The External service connection policy must be enabled on the organization’s Security page.
How to configure
Go to Admin → Agent and open the agent you want to connect to an external service.
Open the Security tab.
In External service connection, turn on Allow external service connection.
If the agent is Enabled, A2A Endpoint, Agent Card URL, and Manage Access Token are displayed.
Copy the A2A Endpoint or Agent Card URL depending on what the external service requires.
In Manage Access Token, issue an A2A Access Token and register it as the authentication credential in the external service.
Values to register in the external service
Item | Description
A2A Endpoint | The endpoint where the external service sends messages to the agent.
Agent Card URL | The URL the external service uses to check the agent name, description, supported capabilities, and endpoint information.
A2A Access Token | The credential used by the external service to call the agent. It can be used as a Bearer token or with the X-A2A-Token header.
External service connection information is displayed only when the organization policy and the agent-level setting are both enabled and the agent is in the Enabled state. If the agent is disabled, it cannot be called from external services.

chunks.heading: Share Scope Settings
chunks.text:
An item for setting agent sharing scope with the following two sharing ranges:
All Users: All members of the organization can access this agent
Specific Users: Select specific users by searching for them by name or email to allow access to the agent.
In organizations where tag-based sharing is enabled, you can select user tags to define the agent’s share scope. By managing user tags by department, role, or project, you can make agents available to the right audience without adding users one by one.

chunks.heading: Agent chat-only Link
chunks.text:
You can provide a chat-only link that opens a specific organization agent directly. Users who receive the link go straight to that agent’s chat screen instead of the agent settings page.
You can configure link access permissions together.
This is useful for customer support, internal FAQs, approval requests, and other workflows where users should talk to a specific agent immediately.
When the share scope changes, the set of users who can access the link changes as well.

chunks.heading: Agent Library
chunks.text: The agent library is a feature that allows organizations to install and use pre-built Built-in agents.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
Pre-configured Agents: Provides agents optimized for specific tasks or domains
Immediately Usable: All configurations are completed for immediate use after installation

chunks.heading: Installation and Usage
chunks.text:
Agent Selection: Select desired agent from the library
Installation: Click “Install” button to install agent in the organization
Configuration: Configure MCP Tool integration and authentication as needed
Activation: Activate agent to share with users

chunks.heading: Agent Usage in User Interface
chunks.text:
When administrators set tool authentication methods belonging to agents to “Require User Authentication”, users need to directly input configuration information or authenticate in the Configuration tab of the detail page
For detailed user agent usage guide, refer to User Guide > Agents.

chunks.heading: Audit Logs
chunks.text: The audit log page allows you to view and manage all important events that occur within your organization. You can track user activities, system changes, security-related events, and more to enhance your organization’s security and compliance.

chunks.heading: Viewing Log List
chunks.text:
On the audit log page, you can view a chronologically sorted list of events. Each log entry includes the following information:
Time: When the event occurred
User: Information about the user who triggered the event
Event Information: Type and detailed information about the event that occurred

chunks.heading: Event Type Filter
chunks.text: You can view only specific types of events. Select the desired event type from the dropdown menu to display only logs of that type.

chunks.heading: User Tag Filter
chunks.text:
You can filter and view activities of users with specific tags assigned.
Search and Select: Quickly find specific tags using the search bar at the top of the filter area.
Multi-Select: Select multiple tags simultaneously for complex filtering.
Select All/Deselect All: Use the Select All option to select or deselect all tags at once.

chunks.heading: Exporting Audit Logs
chunks.text: Click Export to download audit logs that match the current search conditions as a file. A password is required when running the export.

chunks.heading: Event Types
chunks.text: The event types tracked in the audit log are as follows:

chunks.heading: organization.invite.sent
chunks.text: This event occurs when an organization administrator invites a new user to the organization. When an invitation email is sent, it is automatically recorded, including information about the user who sent the invitation and the invited email address.

chunks.heading: organization.user.added
chunks.text: This event occurs when an invited user accepts the invitation and successfully joins the organization. You can track when new members are added to the organization.

chunks.heading: organization.user.removed
chunks.text: This event occurs when an organization administrator removes an existing user from the organization. Information about both the administrator who performed the removal and the removed user is recorded.

chunks.heading: organization.user.role.changed
chunks.text: This event occurs when a user’s permission role is changed within the organization. Both previous and new role information is recorded together, allowing you to track permission change history.

chunks.heading: auth.login.success
chunks.text: This event occurs when a user successfully logs into the system. Login time, IP address, and user information are recorded to manage access history.

chunks.heading: auth.logout
chunks.text: This event occurs when a user logs out of the system. Session termination time and user information are recorded.

chunks.heading: auth.password.changed
chunks.text: This is a security event that occurs when a user changes their password. It is recorded as an important activity for strengthening account security.

chunks.heading: organization.name.changed
chunks.text: This event occurs when the organization’s name is changed. When you modify the name in organization settings, both the previous and new names are recorded to track organization information change history.

chunks.heading: organization.id.changed
chunks.text: This event occurs when the organization’s unique identifier (ID) is changed. Organization identifier changes are important configuration changes that require administrator privileges, and both before and after ID information is recorded.

chunks.heading: organization.owner.changed
chunks.text: This event occurs when organization ownership is transferred to another user. Information about both the previous owner and the new owner is recorded, tracking the highest authority changes in the organization.

chunks.heading: organization.user.add.failure
chunks.text: This event occurs when an attempt to add a user to the organization fails. It is recorded along with failure reasons such as insufficient permissions, duplicate invitations, or system errors to help with problem resolution.

chunks.heading: mcp.integration.created
chunks.text: This event occurs when a new MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration is created. When a new connection setup with an external service is completed, it is recorded, including integration name and configuration information.

chunks.heading: mcp.integration.updated
chunks.text: This event occurs when the settings of an existing MCP integration are modified. When integration-related settings such as connection information, authentication settings, or permissions are updated, they are recorded along with the changes.

chunks.heading: mcp.integration.deleted
chunks.text: This event occurs when an MCP integration is deleted. It is recorded when disconnecting from external services or removing integrations that are no longer in use, tracking integration management history.

chunks.heading: mcp.preset.created
chunks.text: This event occurs when a new MCP preset is created. When frequently used integration settings are saved as templates, it is recorded, including preset name and included configuration information.

chunks.heading: mcp.preset.updated
chunks.text: This event occurs when an existing MCP preset is modified. When settings or names included in the preset are changed, they are recorded along with the modifications to track preset management history.

chunks.heading: mcp.preset.deleted
chunks.text: This event occurs when an MCP preset is deleted. It is recorded when removing presets that are no longer in use, and the deleted preset information is preserved.

chunks.heading: llm.credit.limit.exceeded
chunks.text: This event occurs when the organization’s LLM usage credits exceed the set limit. It is recorded to prevent excessive usage and for cost management, including information about when the limit was exceeded and usage amounts.

chunks.heading: llm.message.failure
chunks.text: This event occurs when message processing sent to the LLM fails. It is recorded along with failure reasons such as network errors, API limit exceeded, or invalid requests to help with problem diagnosis.

chunks.heading: llm.message.received
chunks.text: This event occurs when a response message is successfully received from the LLM. You can track conversation flow and response times, and it is used for system performance monitoring.

chunks.heading: llm.message.sent
chunks.text: This event occurs when a user’s message is successfully sent to the LLM. Request time and message information are recorded to analyze usage patterns.

chunks.heading: llm.tool.call.attempted
chunks.text: This event occurs when the LLM attempts to call a specific tool or function. Tool usage attempts such as MCP integration or external API calls are recorded to track system activity.

chunks.heading: llm.tool.call.failure
chunks.text: This event occurs when an LLM tool call fails. It is recorded along with failure reasons such as integration errors, insufficient permissions, or timeouts to provide information needed for problem resolution.

chunks.heading: llm.tool.call.success
chunks.text: This event occurs when an LLM tool call is successfully completed. Information about the called tool and execution results is recorded to track successful integration activities.

chunks.heading: Log Format Examples
chunks.text: Audit logs are stored in JSON format and have the following structure:

chunks.heading: User Login Success
User Role Change
MCP Integration Creation
Billing
chunks.text: Administrators can check the organization’s subscription plan and credit status on the Billing page.

chunks.heading: Current Plan
chunks.text:
The Current Plan card shows the plan information currently applied to the organization.
Plan name: The currently applied plan, such as Trial, Starter, Team, or Enterprise
Monthly fee: Monthly subscription amount
Period: The period during which the current plan applies
Next billing date: The next scheduled billing date
Plan changes are not currently supported. If you want to change your plan, please contact aip@querypie.com.

chunks.heading: Credits
chunks.text:
The Credits card shows the total credits available to the organization and their detailed breakdown.
Additional credits: Credits purchased separately
Remaining plan credits: Credits included in the current plan that have not been used yet
Used plan credits: Credits already used from the current plan
Event credits: Credits granted through events
Granted credits: Credits granted to the organization by an administrator
Scheduled event credits / scheduled granted credits: Credits scheduled to be granted later
The credit breakdown is also displayed as a bar chart. If the plan has expired, credit usage may be restricted.
In mobile environments, subscription and billing settings can only be viewed.
Credit usage limits can be managed on the Credit limits page.

chunks.heading: Credits History
chunks.text: The Credits History menu lets you view credit transaction history in the organization, including credit charges, usage, refunds, expirations, adjustments, and more.

chunks.heading: Filtering Credits History
chunks.text:
You can filter credit transaction history by the following conditions.
User email: View credit transaction history for a specific user.
Transaction type: Select from all transactions, charge, usage, refund, expiration, adjustment, overuse, or deletion.
Date range: View records for the last 7 days, last 30 days, last 3 months, or a custom date range.

chunks.heading: Viewing Credits History
chunks.text:
The history table shows the main information for each credit transaction.
Date: The date and time when the transaction occurred
User: The user associated with the transaction
Event type: The transaction type, such as charge, usage, or refund
Credits: Credits increased or deducted
Balance after transaction: The credit balance after the transaction
Credit type: The credit source, such as plan, additional, event, Free PoC, PoC, Production, or Partner
Deduction reason: The reason credits were used or changed
When source information is available, the following items are also displayed.
Source type: The usage type where the credit occurred, such as personal agent, organization agent, automation, or general chat
Source name: The name of the target where the credit occurred
Source ID: The ID that identifies the target where the credit occurred
Expand each row to view detailed information for that credit transaction. If there is no detail, No details available is displayed.

chunks.heading: Downloading Credits History
chunks.text:
Administrators can download the queried credit usage history as a CSV file.
On the Credits History page, set the user email, transaction type, and date range filters.
Click CSV Download.
Enter the ZIP password.
When the download starts, save the compressed file and open it with the password you entered.
The CSV download reflects the currently selected user email, transaction type, and date range conditions. You can specify a download period of up to 31 days.

chunks.heading: Responses Stopped by the Recursion Limit
chunks.text:
If tool calls or step execution run too long and reach the recursion limit, response generation may stop. In this case, the credits used for that turn are restored, and the chat screen displays a notice that the credits will be restored.
Administrators can filter Credits History by the Refund transaction type to check restoration records. If credits for the same turn have already been restored, they are not restored again.

chunks.heading: Credit limits
chunks.text: Administrators can use the Credit limits page to set credit usage limits for organization users. You can set a default limit that applies to all users, and apply individual limits to users who need separate management.

chunks.heading: Default Limit
chunks.text:
The default limit is the credit usage limit applied to all users in the organization.
You can configure the following items for the default limit.
Period: Select the limit period from daily, weekly, or monthly.
Limit type: Allow unlimited usage, or enter a fixed credit limit.
Usage is counted by the following periods, and usage resets at the end of each period.
Period | Usage window | Reset time
Daily | 00:00 to 23:59 every day | 00:00 UTC the next day
Weekly | Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 | 00:00 UTC the next Monday
Monthly | 00:00 on the 1st to 23:59 on the last day of each month | 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the next month
The times above are based on UTC.
Changing the default limit may reset existing individual limits.

chunks.heading: Individual Limits
chunks.text:
An individual limit is a credit usage limit applied to a specific user instead of the default limit. Add an individual limit when a user needs to be managed with a different limit from the default.
To add an individual limit, click Add individual limit, select users, and set the limit. In the user selection step, you can filter targets by user name, email, or user tag.
The same individual limit can be applied to selected users at once.

chunks.heading: Managing Individual Limits
chunks.text:
The individual limits list shows each user’s usage and limit. You can edit or remove an individual limit from each user’s action menu.
When an individual limit is removed, the organization’s default limit is applied to that user again.

chunks.heading: Behavior When a Limit Is Reached
chunks.text: When a user’s credit usage reaches the configured limit, additional credit usage may be restricted. Users with an individual limit are restricted based on the individual limit, and users without one are restricted based on the default limit.

chunks.heading: Data Loss Prevention Logs
chunks.text: The DLP Log page allows you to view and analyze all sensitive data detection events that occurred within your organization. You can enhance data security by tracking sensitive information detected in real-time from user input data and LLM response data.

chunks.heading: DLP Log Overview
chunks.text:
DLP logs provide the following information:
Detection Event Tracking: Records all events where sensitive data was detected in chronological order.
Detailed Analysis: Provides detailed information including detected data types, categories, and confidence levels.
Filtering and Search: Filter logs by various conditions and quickly find specific events.

chunks.heading: Basic Filters
chunks.text: The DLP log page provides various filters to help you efficiently find desired events.

chunks.heading: 1. Date Range Filter
chunks.text:
View only events that occurred during a specific period.
Click the date range button to select start and end dates.
By default, it is set to today’s date.
Click the Apply Filter button to apply the filter.

chunks.heading: 2. User Search
chunks.text:
Search for specific user events by name or email.
Enter a user name or email in the search box.
Autocomplete suggestions appear as you type.
You can also search by the username part or domain part of an email.

chunks.heading: 3. Actions Filter
chunks.text:
Filter by the type of action taken on detected sensitive data.
Action Types:
Sensitive Data Sent: Sensitive data was detected but transmission was allowed
Sensitive Data Blocked: Sensitive data was detected and transmission was blocked
How to use the filter:
Click the Actions dropdown.
Use Select All / Deselect All to select/deselect all.
Check/uncheck individual action types.

chunks.heading: 4. Categories / Types Filter
chunks.text:
Filter detected data using a tree structure of categories and types. Data types are nested under their parent categories, displayed in a hierarchical structure.
Main Categories and Sub-types:
Credential
Auth Token, AWS Credentials, Basic Auth Header, Encryption Key, GCP API Key, HTTP Cookie, JSON Web Token, OAuth Client Secret, Password, Security Data, SSL Certificate, Storage Signed URL, Tink Keyset
Government ID
Driver’s licenses, passports, national ID numbers from various countries (e.g., Korea RRN, US Social Security Number, Japan Individual Number, etc.)
Financial ID
Credit Card Number, CVV Number, IBAN Code, Japan Bank Account, etc.
Medical ID
Medical ID, Medical Record Number, etc.
PII (Personal Identifiable Information)
Email Address, Phone Number, Person Name, IP Address, Street Address, etc.
SPII (Sensitive Personal Identifiable Information)
Other highly sensitive personal identifiable information
Technical ID
IP Address, MAC Address, etc.
How to use the filter:
Click the Categories / Types dropdown.
Use the search box to quickly find categories or data types by name.
Category Selection: Checking a category automatically selects all sub-types under that category.
Individual Type Selection: Click the arrow icon next to a category to expand the tree, then check/uncheck specific types individually.
Use the tree structure to filter by entire categories or specific types selectively.

chunks.heading: 5. Likelihood Filter
chunks.text:
Filter by the confidence level of sensitive data detection.
Confidence Levels:
HIGH: High confidence (95% or higher) - Red indicator
MEDIUM: Medium confidence (70-95%) - Orange indicator
LOW: Low confidence (below 70%) - Green indicator
How to use the filter:
Click the Likelihood dropdown.
Check/uncheck desired confidence levels.

chunks.heading: Clear Button
chunks.text:
The Clear button appears when filters are active.
Clicking the Clear button resets all filters to their default state.
Search terms, selected filters, and date range are all reset.

chunks.heading: Exporting DLP Logs
chunks.text: Click Export to download DLP logs that match the current search conditions as a file. A password is required when running the export.

chunks.heading: Table Columns
chunks.text:
The log table consists of the following columns:
Column | Description
Timestamp | Event occurrence time
User | User who triggered the event
Action | Action taken (Sent/Blocked)
Reason | Reason for action (False Positive, Business Requirement, etc.)
Data Types | Detected data types (shows up to 3, rest shown as +N)
Categories | Data categories (shows up to 3, rest shown as +N)
Max Likelihood | Highest confidence level among detected data
Details | Button to expand/collapse details

chunks.heading: Viewing Details
chunks.text:
Click on any log row to expand detailed information.
Detail Information Table:
Data Type: Specific data type detected
Category: Categories the data type belongs to
Likelihood: Confidence level for individual data type
Multiple types of sensitive data can be detected in a single event, and you can check the confidence level and category information for each.

chunks.heading: Result Display
chunks.text:
The number of currently displayed events and total events are shown at the top of the table.
Example: “Showing 8 of 8 events” - Total events before filtering
Example: “Showing 3 of 8 events” - Matched events after filtering

chunks.heading: Sensitive Data Sent Events
chunks.text:
Cases where sensitive data was detected but transmission was allowed for legitimate reasons.
Example 1: GCP API Key Detection
User: user@email.com
Action: Sensitive Data Sent
Reason: False Positive
Detected Data Types: GCP_API_KEY, EMAIL_ADDRESS
Categories: CREDENTIAL, PII
Max Likelihood: HIGH (95%)
Example 2: Phone Number Detection
User: mike.chen@company.com
Action: Sensitive Data Sent
Reason: Business Requirement
Detected Data Types: PHONE_NUMBER
Categories: PII
Max Likelihood: MEDIUM (89%)

chunks.heading: Sensitive Data Blocked Events
chunks.text:
Cases where sensitive data was detected and transmission was blocked.
Example 1: Credit Card Number Detection
User: user@email.com
Action: Sensitive Data Blocked
Reason: - (Blocked)
Detected Data Types: CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER
Categories: FINANCIAL_ID
Max Likelihood: HIGH (87%)
Example 2: External Email Address Detection
User: jane.smith@company.com
Action: Sensitive Data Blocked
Reason: - (Blocked)
Detected Data Types: EMAIL_ADDRESS
Categories: PII
Max Likelihood: MEDIUM (92%)

chunks.heading: References
chunks.text: For detailed information about data types detected by the DLP system, please refer to the Google Cloud DLP InfoTypes Reference .

chunks.heading: Security Auditing
chunks.text:
Regularly review DLP logs to monitor sensitive data leakage attempts.
Focus on Action: Sensitive Data Blocked events to identify security threats.
Prioritize Max Likelihood: HIGH events as they are more likely to be actual sensitive data.

chunks.heading: False Positive Management
chunks.text:
If Reason: False Positive events occur frequently, you may need to adjust DLP settings.
Visit the DLP Management page to disable unnecessary data types or modify custom patterns.

chunks.heading: User Training
chunks.text:
If a specific user frequently attempts to transmit sensitive data, security training may be needed.
Use the user search feature to track individual user event history.

chunks.heading: Compliance
chunks.text:
Use the date range filter to extract logs for a specific period and create compliance reports.
Use the Categories filter to understand the handling status of specific types of sensitive data (e.g., MEDICAL_ID, FINANCIAL_ID).

chunks.heading: Edge Tunnel Management
chunks.text: Manage your organization’s Edge Tunnels and set up secure connections for tunneling.

chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: Edge Tunnels provide secure connections between your organization’s secure network and QueryPie AIP. Administrators can manage both organization Edge Tunnels and personal Edge Tunnels, each serving different purposes.

chunks.heading: Administrator Login
chunks.text: Log in with an administrator account.

chunks.heading: Navigate to Menu
chunks.text: Click SECURITY SETTINGS > Edge Tunnel in the left menu.

chunks.heading: Verify Page
chunks.text: The Edge Tunnel management page will be displayed.

chunks.heading: Organization Edge Tunnel Overview
chunks.text: Organization Edge Tunnels are tunnels that allow multiple servers to connect as a group using the same authentication key. Only organization administrators can create Edge Tunnel groups. (Enterprise Plan only)

chunks.heading: Select Tab
chunks.text: Select the Organization Tunnels tab.

chunks.heading: Click Create Button
chunks.text: Click the Create Organization Tunnel button.

chunks.heading: Enter Tunnel Alias
chunks.text:
Enter a tunnel group name in the Tunnel Alias field.
Only alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores are allowed (no spaces)
Examples: production-cluster, dev-environment, etc.

chunks.heading: Complete Tunnel Creation
chunks.text: Click the check button after entering the information to create the tunnel.

chunks.heading: Connecting Organization Edge Tunnel
chunks.text: After creating the tunnel, a command to run on the server will be provided:

chunks.heading: Click Install Button
chunks.text: Click the Install Edge Tunnel button.

chunks.heading: Copy Command
chunks.text:
Copy the displayed command:
npx -y @querypie/mcp@latest tunnel link '<tunnel-key>'

chunks.heading: Execute Command on Server
chunks.text: Run the copied command in the terminal of the server you want to connect.

chunks.heading: Verify Connection
chunks.text: Once the tunnel is successfully connected, server information will be displayed in the Connected Servers list.

chunks.heading: Checking Connected Server Information
chunks.text:
For each connected server, you can check the following information:
Server Name: Identifier of the connected server
IP Address: Server’s IP address
OS Information: Operating system and version information
Created Date: Date when the server was connected to the tunnel

chunks.heading: Personal Edge Tunnel Overview
chunks.text: Personal Edge Tunnels are tunnels created and managed by individual users. Administrators can monitor and manage all personal Edge Tunnels within the organization.

chunks.heading: Check List
chunks.text:
A list of all personal Edge Tunnels within the organization will be displayed.
The following information is displayed for each tunnel:
Tunnel Identifier: Unique tunnel ID
Username: User who created the tunnel
IP Address: IP address of the connected client
OS Information: Client’s operating system information
Created Date: Date when the tunnel was created

chunks.heading: Force Terminating Personal Edge Tunnel
chunks.text: You can force terminate personal Edge Tunnels when necessary.

chunks.heading: Click Delete Button
chunks.text: Click the delete button (🗑️) on the right side of the tunnel row you want to delete.

chunks.heading: Display Confirmation Dialog
chunks.text: A deletion confirmation dialog will be displayed.

chunks.heading: Verify Tunnel Information
chunks.text:
Verify the following information:
Tunnel Alias: Identifier of the tunnel to be deleted
Type: Tunnel type (Personal)
Created At: Tunnel creation time

chunks.heading: Check Warnings
chunks.text:
Check the warnings in the Warning section:
All active connections will be terminated
Integration settings using this tunnel may fail
This action is permanent and cannot be undone

chunks.heading: Confirm Deletion
chunks.text: Click the Delete Tunnel button to confirm the deletion.

chunks.heading: Using Edge Tunnel in Sandbox
chunks.text:
When a Skill or tool running in Sandbox needs to access a local PC or internal network resource, it can use Edge Tunnel. This lets users connect Sandbox tasks to resources that cannot be accessed directly from the outside, such as local development servers, internal APIs, or VPN-only services.
Usage flow:
In general chat or personal agents, the user enables Edge Tunnel.
In organization agents, the administrator configures Edge Tunnel Scope under the Skill.
The user asks in chat using the http://localhost.tunnel:<port>/... format.
For example, to connect to localhost:3000 on a local PC, the user can ask:
Please connect to localhost.tunnel:3000 and proceed.
If Web Search is enabled, or if a Web Search MCP such as Tavily is connected to an organization agent, a localhost.tunnel request may be treated as a web address lookup. In this case, disable Web Search or add the instruction, “Please connect using the internal skill.”

chunks.heading: Checking Connection Status
chunks.text:
Green dot: Tunnel is active and normally connected
Number of connected servers: Shows the number of servers connected to each organization tunnel

chunks.heading: Tunnel Management Best Practices
chunks.text:
Naming Convention: Write tunnel aliases to clearly indicate their purpose
Regular Inspection: Regularly clean up unnecessary personal tunnels
Security Management: Keep tunnel authentication keys secure
Monitoring: Regularly check the status of connected servers

chunks.heading: Precautions
chunks.text:
Only organization administrators can create organization Edge Tunnels
All connections will be immediately terminated when deleting tunnels
Deleted tunnels cannot be recovered, so decide carefully
Tunnel connection status is updated in real-time

chunks.heading: Knowledge Management
chunks.text:
Knowledge source management through Knowledge Bundles and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) configuration
Knowledge Bundle and Source management is only available to users with Owner and Admin permissions in the organization. General users can only use Agents connected to the Knowledge, but cannot access the Knowledge itself.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
Knowledge Bundle creation and management
File upload capability
Add SharePoint file sources
External source authentication management
Vector embedding-based indexing
RAG service integration

chunks.heading: Knowledge Bundle
chunks.text: Knowledge Bundle is a component that groups knowledge sources referenced by Agents into a single unit. It connects various data such as files, documents, and code repositories, and supports their utilization in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) by indexing them based on vector embeddings.

chunks.heading: Knowledge Source
chunks.text: Refers to files or external data sources (CSV, PDF, GitHub, etc.).

chunks.heading: RAG Service
chunks.text: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) service is provided.

chunks.heading: Bundle List View
chunks.text:
You can view all Knowledge Bundles created at the organizational level as a list.
Display Information:
Name: Bundle name
Description: Description
Sources: Number of connected Knowledge Sources
Status: Indexing status of the entire bundle
Search Function:
Filterable by name

chunks.heading: Bundle Creation
chunks.text:
Click ”+ Create Bundle” button
Enter the following information:
Name (Required): Bundle name
Description: Bundle description
Chunk Size: The chunk size used when splitting documents into searchable units
Overlap: The amount of content to overlap between adjacent chunks
Click “Create” button
A single Knowledge Bundle can contain up to 10 documents.

chunks.heading: Bundle Detail Management
chunks.text:
In the Bundle detail page, you can view and manage the following information:
Bundle Information:
Bundle name and description
Bundle status (INDEXED, Failed, etc.)
Knowledge Sources List:
Detailed information of connected sources
Indexing status of each source
Main Actions:
”+ Add Source”: Add new source
“More Actions”: Additional management features
Individual source management (edit, delete, etc.)

chunks.heading: Supported Source Types
chunks.text: Currently, File upload and SharePoint sources are supported.

chunks.heading: File Upload
chunks.text:
Currently supported file upload functionality:
Supported Formats:
.pdf
.txt, .md, .markdown
.html
.doc, .docx
.csv, .xls, .xlsx
Limitations:
Maximum size: 50MB
Click “Start” button after file upload to begin indexing
Source name can be entered (default: filename)
You can adjust Chunk Size and Overlap as needed to configure the indexing method.

chunks.heading: Add SharePoint Source
chunks.text:
You can import files stored in SharePoint as Knowledge Sources and add them to a Knowledge Bundle.
Add procedure
On the Knowledge Bundle detail page, click + Add Source.
Select the SharePoint source.
Select the SharePoint account to use, or connect a new account.
Browse SharePoint sites, drives, and folders, then select the files to import.
Click Import to add the selected files as Knowledge Sources.
Start indexing the imported sources.
Supported formats
.pdf
.doc, .docx
.txt, .md
.html
.csv, .xlsx
.json
Limitations
Maximum size per file: 50 MB
OneNote notebooks cannot be imported as Knowledge Sources.
Unsupported file formats cannot be selected.
A file already added to the same bundle cannot be imported again.

chunks.heading: Update SharePoint Source
chunks.text:
Changes to the original SharePoint file are checked automatically. By default, the original file is checked about once every hour. When a change is detected, the Knowledge Source list shows the Source Changed status and an Update button.
Click Update for the SharePoint source marked Source Changed.
The latest file from SharePoint is imported again and replaces the existing source file.
When the update is complete, index the source again so the latest content is reflected in search.
If the stored SharePoint authentication has expired or token renewal fails, a Reconnect SharePoint Account notice is displayed. In this case, authenticate again with the account that was previously connected, then retry the update. Re-authenticating with a different SharePoint account may fail because the existing file and account do not match.

chunks.heading: External Source Authentication Management
chunks.text:
In Authentication Management on the Knowledge Management page, you can manage external service accounts used for Knowledge Sources.
Available actions in Authentication Management
Check the list of connected SharePoint accounts
Check account status: Connected, Re-authentication Required, Expired, Disconnected
Re-authenticate accounts that are expired or require re-authentication
Disconnect accounts that are no longer used
Accounts with connected Knowledge Sources can be disconnected after deleting the sources.

chunks.heading: Chunk Size and Overlap Settings
chunks.text:
You can set Chunk Size and Overlap when creating a Knowledge Bundle or adding a Source.
Chunk Size: The size used to split a document into searchable units. A smaller value enables more granular search, while a larger value allows longer context to be retrieved at once.
Overlap: The amount of content included in both adjacent chunks. Increasing this value can reduce context loss around paragraph boundaries.
For documents where long context should be preserved, increasing Overlap is useful. For short, structured documents, setting a smaller Chunk Size can help find the desired information more narrowly.

chunks.heading: Knowledge Bundle Status
chunks.text:
Status | Description
None | When there are no Sources in the Bundle
Uploaded | When there is at least one Source in the Bundle that is not indexed
Indexing | When there is at least one Source in the Bundle that is currently being indexed
Indexed | When all Sources in the Bundle have completed indexing
Failed | When there is at least one Source in the Bundle that failed indexing

chunks.heading: Knowledge Source Status
chunks.text:
Status | Description
Start | Before indexing
Indexing | During indexing
Indexed | Indexing completed
Failed | When indexing failed

chunks.heading: Deletion Restrictions
chunks.text:
Knowledge Bundles and Sources cannot be deleted when their status is Indexing
In this case, the Delete button is disabled

chunks.heading: Knowledge Source Deletion
chunks.text:
Can be deleted even if connected to Bundle/Agent
Bundle is maintained but search scope is reduced
Source-related content is excluded from RAG results when Agent is executed
The source’s index (RAG vector) is also removed
Deletion Confirmation Message:
“Deleting it will reduce the bundle’s coverage and may affect linked agents. Do you want to continue?”

chunks.heading: Knowledge Bundle Deletion
chunks.text:
Bundle cannot be deleted if connected Agents exist
Bundle can be deleted after removing all sources within the Bundle
Deletion Confirmation Message:
“Deleting this bundle may affect linked agents. Do you want to proceed?”

chunks.heading: Re-indexing
chunks.text:
Re-indexing possible at source level
Re-indexing possible for all sources

chunks.heading: Important Notes
chunks.text:
Knowledge Bundles serve as the knowledge foundation for Agents, so they must be managed carefully
Deletion may affect connected Agents, so prior confirmation is necessary
Deletion is not possible during indexing status, so proceed after completion
Check the file size limit (50MB) and the Chunk Size and Overlap settings when uploading files

chunks.heading: LLM Models
chunks.text: Manage which models this organization can use.

chunks.heading: Accessing the Page
chunks.text: Admin → AI&MCP Settings → LLM Models

chunks.heading: Configuring Model Access
chunks.text:
The models available to your organization are displayed in a table. Use the toggle switch on the right side of each model to enable or disable it.
Enabled: Organization members can select and use this model in chat.
Disabled: This model is removed from the model selection list in chat.

chunks.heading: Enabling Auto Router
chunks.text:
Auto Router is a model that automatically selects a model based on the user’s request and conversation context. It is disabled by default. To let organization members use Auto Router in chat, an administrator must enable it first.
To enable Auto Router, turn on the Auto Router toggle in the model list, then click Save Changes in the top-right corner. After the change is saved, Auto Router appears in the chat model selector for organization members.
The models used for each Auto Router tier are currently set by the system and cannot be changed from this page.

chunks.heading: Behavior When a Model Is Disabled
chunks.text:
Chat: If a model previously selected by a user is disabled, they are automatically switched to the default model.
Agent: Only models permitted by the organization are shown in agent settings. If a model assigned to an agent is disabled, execution is blocked and an error is returned at runtime.

chunks.heading: Saving Changes
chunks.text:
After making changes, click the Save Changes button in the top-right corner to apply them.
Note: If you attempt to leave the page with unsaved changes, a warning will appear to prevent accidental data loss.

chunks.heading: Summary
chunks.text:
Enable or disable individual LLM models per organization using toggle switches
Disabled models are immediately removed from the chat model selection list
Changes must be saved by clicking Save Changes to take effect

chunks.heading: MCP Integration Management
chunks.text: MCP Integration Management is a feature that allows you to manage MCP servers used within your organization.

chunks.heading: MCP Integration Types
chunks.text:
MCP integrations within an organization are categorized into two main types:
Built-in MCP Integrations: MCP integrations provided by default
Configured MCP Integrations: MCP integrations pre-configured by organization administrators and provided to users

chunks.heading: Built-in MCP Integration Management
chunks.text:
In the admin console, you can view and manage the list of built-in MCP integrations.
The management tasks you can perform for built-in MCP integrations are as follows:
Select MCP integration activation status: When an integration is deactivated, all previously installed integrations are deactivated and removed from the list of installable integrations.
MCP Access Control: For activated integrations, you can set the list of tools to allow for users within the organization.
Load tool list: For integrations such as Custom Remote MCP where the server dynamically provides the tool list, you can load the tool list from the detail page.

chunks.heading: Configured MCP Integration Management
chunks.text:
In the admin console, you can view and manage the list of configured MCP integrations.
The management tasks you can perform for configured MCP integrations are as follows:
Create configured MCP integrations: You can create configured MCP integrations.
Supported types: The following types of MCP integration types are supported:
Custom Remote MCP
n8n Chat
n8n Webhook
Dify API Access
Backlog
Redis
Salesforce - Custom
Zendesk
MySQL
MariaDB
PostgreSQL
SQL Server
Oracle Database
ClickHouse
Snowflake
When creating configured MCP integrations, you must enter the necessary configuration information according to the integration type.
By pre-entering authentication information, users can install and use integrations without having to enter authentication information directly.
Select MCP integration activation status: When an integration is deactivated, all previously installed integrations are deactivated and removed from the list of installable integrations.
MCP Access Control: For activated integrations, you can set the list of tools to allow for users within the organization.
Reuse Client ID / Secret: When editing or re-authenticating an OAuth-based configured integration, existing stored Client information is preserved if you do not enter a new Client ID / Secret.

chunks.heading: MCP Integration Activation/Deactivation
chunks.text:
MCP integrations are activated by default, and activated integrations can be freely installed by users from the Integration menu.
When an MCP integration is deactivated, all previously installed integrations are deactivated and removed from the list of installable integrations.
Even if previously installed integrations were added to MCP Presets, tools cannot be called.
When an MCP integration is reactivated, existing user settings are restored to their original state.

chunks.heading: Changing Activation Status from MCP Integration List
chunks.text:
Find the MCP integration you want to change the activation status for in the list table within the MCP Integration Management page.
Click the more options button on the right to display the dropdown menu.
Click the menu button to change the activation status.

chunks.heading: Changing Activation Status from MCP Detail Page
chunks.text:
Click an item on the MCP Integration Management page to navigate to the detail page.
Click the more options button on the right side of the header to display the dropdown menu.
Click the menu button to change the activation status.

chunks.heading: MCP Access Control
chunks.text:
MCP Access Control is a feature that allows you to set the list of tools to allow for users within the organization for activated MCP integrations.
As of September 8, 2025, the MCP Access Control feature can define the list of tools to allow for all organization users, and is scheduled to be updated to support ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) in September 2025.

chunks.heading: Adding Access Policy
chunks.text: Click the Add Policy button on the MCP integration detail page to display the new access policy addition modal.

chunks.heading: Adding New Access Policy
chunks.text: Enter the policy name and description, specify the users to allow for this policy with tags, then select the tools you want to allow in this policy and save.

chunks.heading: Confirming Added Access Policy
chunks.text: You can confirm the added policy on the MCP integration detail page.

chunks.heading: Load Tool List
chunks.text:
For integrations such as Custom Remote MCP where the server dynamically provides the tool list, you can load the tool list from the MCP detail page.
Use Load Tool List in cases such as:
New tools have been added to the MCP server
Existing tool names or descriptions have changed on the MCP server
The tool list could not be loaded, or only part of it was displayed, when the integration was created

chunks.heading: Reuse Client ID / Secret
chunks.text:
OAuth-based configured MCP integrations authenticate with the Client ID and Client Secret issued by the external service’s OAuth App. When an administrator stores the Credential entered while registering an MCP as preconfigured, users can use the authentication information configured by the administrator without entering separate Client information.
When an administrator registers a preconfigured MCP, enters the Credential, and completes authentication, a popup asks whether to save this authentication information.
If the administrator chooses to save it, the authentication information is stored and the Authentication setting changes to OAuth / Admin authentication.
To switch to user-specific authentication, click the settings button next to Admin authentication, delete the stored authentication information, and change it to User authentication.
This is useful when multiple users need to use the same OAuth App without entering the Client ID or Client Secret themselves. Conversely, integrations that should connect with each user’s own account permissions can be switched to User authentication so each user completes OAuth authentication directly.

chunks.heading: Sandbox
chunks.text: Manage sandbox environment settings for your organization.

chunks.heading: Allowed Outbound Hosts
chunks.text:
Specify external hosts that are allowed to be accessed from the sandbox. Network requests to unregistered hosts will be blocked.
Supported formats:
Format | Example | Description
Domain | api.example.com | Allow a specific domain
Wildcard | *.google.com | Allow all subdomains
IP Address | 192.168.1.100 | Allow a specific IP
CIDR | 10.0.0.0/24 | Allow an IP range
Port | example.com:8080 | Allow a specific port only
Multiple hosts can be entered separated by commas (,).

chunks.heading: Dynamic Host Allow
chunks.text:
A setting that allows users to immediately grant access to blocked hosts during skill execution.
Enabled (Default): When a skill attempts to access an unregistered host during execution, a prompt asking whether to temporarily allow access is displayed to the user. If the user allows it, access is temporarily granted for that session.
Disabled: Access to unregistered hosts is immediately blocked, and no access prompt is displayed to the user.
Pre-registering frequently used external hosts in Allowed Outbound Hosts allows users to use skills smoothly without receiving access requests each time.

chunks.heading: Saving Settings
chunks.text: After making all setting changes, click the Update Sandbox Settings button to save.

chunks.heading: Security Settings
chunks.text: The Security settings page lets you manage your organization’s security policies and access controls.

chunks.heading: Login and Authentication Security
chunks.text: You can restrict the IP address ranges that are allowed to access organization login. If the allow list is empty, login is allowed from all IP addresses.

chunks.heading: Login IP Access Control List (ACL)
chunks.text:
Enter the IP addresses or CIDR ranges to allow.
Single IP addresses are supported.
CIDR notation can be used to enter IP ranges.
Separate multiple entries with line breaks.
After changing the settings, click Update Login IP ACL to apply them to the organization.

chunks.heading: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
chunks.text: DLP settings let you manage the sensitive data types to detect in user inputs and AI outputs.

chunks.heading: Sensitive Data Type Detection
chunks.text:
You can select the sensitive data types to detect.
Credentials: Passwords, API keys, tokens, certificates, and more
Government ID: Passports, driver’s licenses, resident registration numbers, and more
Sensitive Personal Information (SPII): Financial accounts, credit cards, medical records, and more
Demographic Information: Age, date of birth, person images, and more
Personally Identifiable Information (PII): Names, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, and more
Other Information: Blood type, toll-free numbers, and more
Select the required items, then click Update DLP detection settings to save.

chunks.heading: Custom Regex Patterns
chunks.text:
You can add custom regex patterns to detect sensitive information that your organization needs to manage separately.
InfoType name: A unique identifier for the pattern. It must start with an uppercase letter and can contain only uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores.
Regular expression pattern: The JavaScript regular expression pattern used for detection.
Description: The purpose or example of the pattern.
For detailed configuration of sensitive data types and custom regex patterns, refer to DLP Management.

chunks.heading: Chat History Management
chunks.text: You can set how long organization chat history is retained. Chat history older than the configured retention period is automatically deleted.

chunks.heading: Retention Period Settings
chunks.text:
You can select one of the following options.
Unlimited: Chat history is not automatically deleted.
1 year (365 days)
3 years (1,095 days)
5 years (1,825 days)
10 years (3,650 days)

chunks.heading: How to Change Settings
chunks.text:
Select the retention period from the dropdown.
Click Edit.
The changed retention period is applied to the organization.
Chat history older than the retention period becomes subject to automatic deletion. Check your organization’s security policy and data retention requirements before changing this setting.

chunks.heading: Chat Execution Policy
chunks.text:
Set the default value and upper limit for the organization’s chat recursion limit. Users can set their personal value within the organization upper limit.
Default: The recursion limit applied when the user has not changed the setting.
Upper limit: The highest recursion limit users can select in their personal settings.
Users can adjust the value in Recursion Limit under User Settings, within the range allowed by the organization.

chunks.heading: External Service Connection
chunks.text:
Configure whether external services that support the A2A protocol can call organization agents. This is an organization-wide policy. Administrators must enable this first before external service connection can be allowed for individual agents from each agent’s security tab.
When the organization policy is off, external service connection settings cannot be changed for individual agents. Enable the organization policy only when external services need to call agents, then allow the connection again on the specific agent that should be exposed.

chunks.heading: DLP Management
chunks.text: The DLP (Data Loss Prevention) management page allows you to configure and manage policies for detecting sensitive information in prompt text that users enter in chat. When sensitive information is detected according to the configured policy, QueryPie displays a warning, requires the user to enter a reason, and this log can be reviewed on the DLP Logs page in the Admin console.

chunks.heading: DLP Policy Overview
chunks.text:
The DLP system operates in the following manner:
Prompt Text Inspection: Analyzes prompt text submitted by users.
Sensitive Information Detection: Automatically identifies sensitive information based on configured data type patterns.
Warning and Log Recording: Displays a warning when sensitive information is detected, and records the event in DLP logs when the user submits the prompt after entering a reason.

chunks.heading: Sensitive Data Type Detection Settings
chunks.text: The DLP system can detect 6 major categories of sensitive data. Each category consists of multiple detailed items, which can be individually enabled or disabled according to your organization’s requirements.

chunks.heading: 1. Credentials
chunks.text:
Detects credential information used for system access, such as passwords, API keys, tokens, and certificates.
Included Items (13):
AUTH_TOKEN - Authentication token
AWS_CREDENTIALS - AWS credentials
BASIC_AUTH_HEADER - Basic authentication header
ENCRYPTION_KEY - Encryption key
GCP_API_KEY - GCP API key
HTTP_COOKIE - HTTP cookie
JSON_WEB_TOKEN - JWT token
OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET - OAuth client secret
PASSWORD - Password
SECURITY_DATA - Security data
SSL_CERTIFICATE - SSL certificate
STORAGE_SIGNED_URL - Storage signed URL
TINK_KEYSET - Tink keyset

chunks.heading: 2. Government ID
chunks.text:
Detects government-issued IDs, passports, driver’s licenses, and national identification numbers from countries worldwide.
Included Items (33):
Australia:
AUSTRALIA_DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - Australian driver’s license number
AUSTRALIA_MEDICARE_NUMBER - Australian Medicare number
AUSTRALIA_PASSPORT - Australian passport
AUSTRALIA_TAX_FILE_NUMBER - Australian tax file number
Canada:
CANADA_BC_PHN - Canada BC personal health number
CANADA_DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - Canadian driver’s license number
CANADA_PASSPORT - Canadian passport
CANADA_SOCIAL_INSURANCE_NUMBER - Canadian social insurance number
China and Hong Kong:
CHINA_PASSPORT - Chinese passport
CHINA_RESIDENT_ID_NUMBER - Chinese resident ID number
HONG_KONG_ID_NUMBER - Hong Kong ID number
India:
INDIA_PASSPORT - Indian passport
Indonesia:
INDONESIA_NIK_NUMBER - Indonesian national ID number
INDONESIA_PASSPORT - Indonesian passport
Ireland:
IRELAND_PASSPORT - Irish passport
IRELAND_PPSN - Irish personal public service number
Japan:
JAPAN_DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - Japanese driver’s license number
JAPAN_INDIVIDUAL_NUMBER - Japanese Individual Number (My Number)
JAPAN_PASSPORT - Japanese passport
South Korea:
KOREA_DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - Korean driver’s license number
KOREA_PASSPORT - Korean passport
KOREA_RRN - Korean resident registration number
Taiwan:
TAIWAN_ID_NUMBER - Taiwan ID number
United Kingdom:
UK_PASSPORT - UK passport
United States:
US_DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - US driver’s license number
US_INDIVIDUAL_TAXPAYER_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER - US individual taxpayer identification number

chunks.heading: 2. Government ID
chunks.text:
US_MEDICARE_BENEFICIARY_ID_NUMBER - US Medicare beneficiary ID number
US_PASSPORT - US passport
US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER - US social security number
Other:
DOD_ID_NUMBER - US Department of Defense ID number
DRIVERS_LICENSE_NUMBER - General driver’s license number
GOVERNMENT_ID - General government-issued ID
PASSPORT - General passport

chunks.heading: 3. Sensitive Personal Information (SPII)
chunks.text:
Detects personal information requiring high-level security, such as financial accounts, credit cards, and medical records.
Included Items (12):
CREDIT_CARD_DATA - Credit card data
CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER - Credit card number
CVV_NUMBER - CVV number
FINANCIAL_ACCOUNT_NUMBER - Financial account number
FINANCIAL_ID - Financial ID
IBAN_CODE - IBAN code
ICCID_NUMBER - ICCID number
IMEI_HARDWARE_ID - IMEI hardware ID
IMSI_ID - IMSI ID
JAPAN_BANK_ACCOUNT - Japanese bank account
MEDICAL_ID - Medical ID
MEDICAL_RECORD_NUMBER - Medical record number

chunks.heading: 4. Demographic Information
chunks.text:
Detects demographic information such as age and date of birth.
Included Items (2):
AGE - Age
DATE_OF_BIRTH - Date of birth

chunks.heading: 5. Personal Identifiable Information (PII)
chunks.text:
Detects information that can identify individuals, such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, and IP addresses.
Included Items (15):
EMAIL_ADDRESS - Email address
FEMALE_NAME - Female name
FIRST_NAME - First name
IP_ADDRESS - IP address
LAST_NAME - Last name
MAC_ADDRESS - MAC address
MAC_ADDRESS_LOCAL - Local MAC address
MAC_ADDRESS_UNIVERSAL - Universal MAC address
MALE_NAME - Male name
PERSON_NAME - Full name
PHONE_NUMBER - Phone number

US_VEHICLE_IDENTIFICATION_NUMBER - US vehicle identification number
