chunks.heading: 6. Other Information
chunks.text:
Detects other sensitive information that does not belong to the above categories.
Included Items (2):
BLOOD_TYPE - Blood type
US_TOLLFREE_PHONE_NUMBER - US toll-free phone number

chunks.heading: Check Category Details
chunks.text: Click on each category to expand and view all detailed items included in that category. The category header displays the number of currently selected items and the total number of items. (e.g., 15/17)

chunks.heading: Select All or Individual Items
chunks.text:
Select All: Use the “Select All” checkbox within each category to select or deselect all items in that category at once.
Individual Selection: Check only the items you need individually.

chunks.heading: Save Settings
chunks.text: After selecting all desired data types, click the “Update DLP Detection Settings” button at the bottom of the page to save your settings.

chunks.heading: Expand/Collapse Features
chunks.text:
Expand All: Expand all categories at once to view detailed items.
Collapse All: Collapse all categories for a concise view.

chunks.heading: Custom Regex Pattern Settings
chunks.text: You can define custom regular expression (regex) patterns to detect specific formats of sensitive data according to your organization’s special requirements. For example, you can configure detection for company-specific employee ID formats, project codes, internal document numbers, etc.

chunks.heading: Custom Pattern Components
chunks.text: Each custom pattern consists of three pieces of information:

chunks.heading: InfoType Name (Required)
chunks.text:
A unique identifier for the pattern.
It is recommended to use the UPPERCASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES format.
Examples: EMPLOYEE_ID, PROJECT_CODE, INTERNAL_DOCUMENT_NUMBER

chunks.heading: Regular Expression Pattern (Required)
chunks.text:
A regular expression that defines the pattern of data to detect.
Follows standard JavaScript regular expression syntax.
It is recommended to avoid capture groups for performance.
Example: EMP-[0-9]{6} (Employee ID: EMP-123456 format)
Example: PRJ-[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4} (Project code: PRJ-ABC-1234 format)

chunks.heading: Description (Optional)
chunks.text:
You can add a detailed description of the pattern.
Describing what format of data is detected with examples helps with management.
Example: “Employee ID pattern with format EMP-XXXXXX where X is a digit”

chunks.heading: Add New Pattern
chunks.text: Click the “Add Custom Pattern” button to create a new pattern card.

chunks.heading: Enter Pattern Information
chunks.text:
In the created card, enter the following information:
InfoType Name: Enter the unique name of the pattern (required)
Regular Expression Pattern: Enter the regex pattern (required)
Description: Enter a description of the pattern (optional)

chunks.heading: Pattern Validation
chunks.text: When you enter a regex pattern, it is automatically validated. Invalid regex formats are displayed in red and cannot be saved.

chunks.heading: Save Settings
chunks.text: After entering all patterns correctly, click the “Update DLP Settings” button to save.

chunks.heading: Custom Pattern Management
chunks.text:
Edit Pattern: You can modify information of existing patterns.
Delete Pattern: Click the X button at the top right of each pattern card to delete it.
Manage Multiple Patterns: You can add as many custom patterns as your organization needs.

chunks.heading: Employee ID Pattern
Internal Project Code
Contract Number
References
chunks.text: The DLP system is built based on Google Cloud DLP’s custom infoType format. For more information on writing regex patterns, please refer to the Google Cloud DLP official documentation .

chunks.heading: Precautions
chunks.text:
Performance Considerations: Overly complex regex patterns can affect system performance. Use simple and efficient patterns whenever possible.
Prevent Over-detection: Patterns that are too broad may classify unnecessary data as sensitive information. Test patterns thoroughly before applying them.
Regular Review: Review and update DLP settings whenever your organization’s data protection requirements change.
Avoid Duplicate Pattern Names: InfoType Names must be unique. Do not use duplicate names.

chunks.heading: Skill Management
chunks.text: This feature allows you to register and manage public skills that can be utilized by all agents and users within the organization. Registered skills can be directly connected to agents or cloned by users to their personal skills menu for use.

chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: By deploying verified useful skills, administrators can enhance the overall work efficiency of the organization without requiring individual users to create skills each time.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
Official Library: View verified skills provided by the platform and select which skills to make available to users within the organization.
Public Skill Registration: Register by uploading skill packages in .zip or .skill format.
Agent Integration: Configure specific agents to use the skill.
Allow User Cloning: Allow users to clone administrator skills to their Skills menu for use.
Cloned skills are managed independently from the administrator version.
Even if the administrator updates the original skill, users’ already cloned skills are not affected. Skills modified by users remain unchanged.
When the original skill is updated, users can check the list of skills that need updating in their Skills Library and re-clone the latest version if needed.
Secret Management: Securely register and reference secret information such as API Keys and Access Tokens needed when Skills call external APIs.

chunks.heading: Step 1: Access Skills Menu
chunks.text: Click Skills in the left menu of the admin page.

chunks.heading: Step 2: Add Skill
chunks.text: Click the New Skill button at the top right to enter the skill registration screen.

chunks.heading: Step 3: Upload Skill and Enter Information
chunks.text:
Upload the skill file (.zip, .skill). You can register Skill packages up to 50MB. The skill name and description included in the file will be automatically entered, and you can modify them if necessary.
User Library Visibility: If this option is enabled, users can view and clone the skill in their Skills menu. If disabled, it is used only for agent integration.

chunks.heading: Step 4: Save
chunks.text:
When configuration is complete, click the Save button to finish saving. The registered skill can be confirmed in the list.
Hide/Show: This option allows you to control the visibility in the user Skills Library list. It does not affect the agent Skill settings list.
Download: You can download the skill file in .zip format.
Delete: When deleting a skill, it does not affect skills already cloned by users, but it will be automatically removed from agents currently using the skill.

chunks.heading: Skill Secret Management
chunks.text:
When a Skill needs to call an external API, you can securely manage secret information such as API Keys and Access Tokens. Instead of including secrets directly in Skill code or uploaded files, save them separately and reference them when the Skill runs.
Define secrets in the frontmatter of SKILL.md as follows.
---
name: test-secret-printer
description: Uses TEST_KEY from organization secrets.
secrets:
- ref: ${secrets.TEST_KEY}
---
Add the defined secrets to the table.

chunks.heading: Official Library
chunks.text:
You can manage verified skills provided by the platform. In the Skills menu of the admin page, you can view the official library and select which skills to make available to users within the organization.
Official Library Management:
You can view the list of verified skills provided by the platform.
You can control which skills are used within the organization by enabling/disabling each official library skill.
Network access control for the skill sandbox can be configured on the Sandbox page.

chunks.heading: Importing a Skill from a GitHub URL
chunks.text:
Administrators can import and register a Skill by entering a GitHub repository URL. For private repositories, enter a Personal Access Token if needed.
Click Add from GitHub.
Enter the GitHub repository URL and verify the repository.
Select a branch.
Review the details, then click Import to register the Skill.

chunks.heading: Usage Analytics
chunks.text:
The Usage Analytics page allows you to monitor your organization’s credit usage and MCP tool call activity.
The Usage Analytics page is only accessible to organization Owners and Admins.

chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text: The Usage Analytics page provides insights into your organization’s AI credit usage patterns, enabling efficient resource management.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
View credit usage trends by time period
Analyze active users and average credit consumption
Check detailed usage history by user
View usage by agent
View MCP tool usage statistics

chunks.heading: Data Aggregation
chunks.text:
All usage data is aggregated daily based on UTC 0:00
Data is aggregated and displayed in real-time

chunks.heading: Period Selection
chunks.text:
You can select the time period you want to view at the top of the page.
Last 7 days: Data from today through the past 7 days (default)
Last 30 days: Data from today through the past 30 days
Last 3 months: Data from today through the past 3 months
Custom period: Click the calendar icon to select your desired start and end dates
When you change the period, all areas of the page (summary cards, chart, table, statistics) will be updated to reflect the selected period.

chunks.heading: Summary Cards
chunks.text: At the top of the page, three summary cards display key metrics for the selected period at a glance.

chunks.heading: Total Credits Used
chunks.text:
The total amount of credits consumed by your organization during the selected period.
Aggregates all credit consumption from AI model usage
Includes all credit-consuming activities such as LLM chats and MCP tool calls

chunks.heading: Active Users
chunks.text:
The number of users who consumed credits during the selected period.
Active users are users who have consumed actual credits through LLM chats at least once during the queried period. Users who only logged in are not included.

chunks.heading: Avg Credits per Active User
chunks.text:
The average credit usage per active user.
Formula: Total Credits Used ÷ Number of Active Users
Helps understand the average credit consumption pattern of users

chunks.heading: Daily Usage Trends
chunks.text:
A chart visualizing daily credit usage and MCP call counts during the selected period.
Blue line (Credits Used): Daily credit usage (left Y-axis)
Green line (MCP Calls): Daily MCP tool call count (right Y-axis)
X-axis: Date

chunks.heading: Daily Usage Details
chunks.text: A table showing detailed daily credit usage by user.

chunks.heading: Table Structure
chunks.text:
Date: The date when credits were used
Credits Used: Amount of credits consumed by the user on that date
User: User name and email address
User Tags: List of tags assigned to the user

chunks.heading: Search Function
chunks.text:
You can search by user name or email.
The search function only applies to the Daily Usage Details table and does not affect other areas (summary cards, chart, statistics).

chunks.heading: Credits by Tag
chunks.text:
You can compare credit usage by user tag group.
Tag: The user tag for which usage is aggregated
Credits used: Total credits used by users assigned to the tag
Share: The tag’s share of total organization credit usage
User count: Number of users assigned to the tag
You can filter by tag key, and click View by user to see credit usage by user within the selected tag.

chunks.heading: Notes
chunks.text:
If a user has multiple tags, that user’s credit usage is counted under each tag.
Credit usage is aggregated based on the tags assigned to the user at the time of usage.
The user breakdown in tag details shows only users who used credits during the selected period.

chunks.heading: Top 5 Users by Credits
chunks.text: Shows the top 5 users who consumed the most credits during the selected period.

chunks.heading: Displayed Information
chunks.text:
For each user, the following information is displayed:
Rank: From 1st to 5th place
User name
Credits Used: Total credit consumption
Percentage: User’s percentage of total organization credit usage

chunks.heading: Use Cases
chunks.text:
Identify users with high credit consumption
Analyze usage patterns for resource management
Communicate with individual users about usage when necessary

chunks.heading: Top 5 MCP Tools
chunks.text: Shows the top 5 most frequently called MCP tools during the selected period.

chunks.heading: Displayed Information
chunks.text:
Rank: From 1st to 5th place
Tool name: Name of the MCP tool
Calls: Total number of calls
Percentage: Tool’s percentage of total MCP calls

chunks.heading: Usage by Agent
chunks.text: You can view credit usage by agent in your organization during the selected period.

chunks.heading: Displayed Information
chunks.text:
Agent name: The agent where usage occurred
Agent type: Personal agent or organization agent
Credits used: Credits consumed by the agent during the selected period
Users: Number of users who used the agent

chunks.heading: Use Cases
chunks.text:
Identify frequently used organization agents and prioritize operations.
Review high-usage agents’ Instruction, MCP, and Knowledge configurations to optimize costs.
Check the adoption impact of task-specific agents based on usage.

chunks.heading: Lingo AI
chunks.text:
Lingo AI is an AI Assistant that answers questions using the transcript of a live or ended meeting. You can summarize the entire meeting, identify decisions and action items, or attach selected utterances to focus a question on a specific part of the discussion.
Lingo AI is a Beta feature and uses your organization’s AIP credits when generating an answer.

chunks.heading: Open Lingo AI
chunks.text:
Lingo AI is available from:
A live meeting screen
The detail page of an ended meeting
Select the Lingo AI face icon button on the right side of the meeting screen to open the Lingo AI panel. To minimize the panel, select the collapse button in its header. If you minimize it while an answer is being generated, generation continues and the Lingo AI button indicates when a new answer is available.
On desktop, the transcript and Lingo AI appear side by side. Drag the panel’s left edge to adjust its width. On mobile, Lingo AI opens as a full-width panel.

chunks.heading: Use a suggested question
chunks.text:
A new chat provides frequently used questions. Selecting one sends it immediately.
Suggested question | Description
Meeting summary | Summarizes the key discussion and conclusions.
Decisions | Separates confirmed decisions from unresolved discussion.
Action items | Identifies tasks and deadlines assigned to you without guessing unclear details.

chunks.heading: Ask your own question
chunks.text:
Enter a question in Ask Lingo AI at the bottom of the panel.
Select Send question.
The answer appears progressively as it is generated.
Select Stop response to interrupt an answer in progress. If generation fails, select Try again or send the question again.
Questions work best when they ask for information that can be found in the meeting transcript. For example:
List only the schedule changes discussed in this meeting.
Create a table of follow-up actions, owners, and deadlines.
Separate the customer’s concerns from the responses.

chunks.heading: Attach specific meeting content
chunks.text:
Select one or more utterance blocks in the transcript to attach only that content as a reference for your question. During a live meeting, you can select utterance blocks after their text has been finalized.
Select an utterance block in the meeting transcript.
Select additional utterances if you need more context.
If Lingo AI is minimized, select Ask AI in the selection bar.
Confirm N meeting excerpts attached above the composer.
Enter and send your question.
Select the attachment indicator to review the attached speakers and text. Remove one item with its remove button, or select Clear all selections to remove every attachment.
Attachments narrow the context for a question. If Lingo AI should consider the whole meeting, ask your question without attaching utterances.

chunks.heading: Reset the chat
chunks.text:
After a question and answer exist, select the trash button or the more-actions menu and choose Reset Lingo AI chat.
Resetting deletes all Lingo AI questions and answers for that meeting. It does not delete the original transcript or translations. If an answer is still being generated, wait for it to finish before resetting.

chunks.heading: Lingo AI and AI Summary
chunks.text:
AI Summary on the meeting detail page creates a single result from a predefined template or custom prompt. Lingo AI is designed for free-form questions, follow-up questions, and questions focused on selected utterances.
Feature | Best used for
AI Summary | Creating a formatted summary, minutes, or action-item report in one step
Lingo AI | Exploring the meeting through multiple questions and follow-ups

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
Situation | What to check
An answer could not be generated | Wait briefly, then select Try again or send the question again.
A connection recovery message appears | Wait for the network connection to recover. Lingo checks the completion status automatically.
Credits are insufficient | Add organization credits in AIP, then retry answer generation.

chunks.heading: Calendar
chunks.text: Calendar shows connected calendar events and lets you configure Lingo auto-join for each event.

chunks.heading: Connect calendar
chunks.text:
If no calendar is connected, these connection options appear under Upcoming meetings.
Google Calendar
Microsoft Outlook
After account authorization is completed, only calendar events with meeting URLs are shown in Upcoming meetings. Events without meeting links are not shown because Lingo cannot join them.

chunks.heading: Check upcoming meetings
chunks.text:
Meetings are grouped by date. Each card shows:
Start and end time
Meeting platform: Google Meet, Zoom, MS Teams
Meeting title. If there is no title, (Untitled) is shown.
Recurring event icon
Auto join toggle
For events with Auto join turned on, the selected languages are shown as flag icons on the right side of the card.

chunks.heading: Turn on auto-join
chunks.text:
Turn on Auto join on the event card.
Select Source Language. You can select up to three languages.
If translation is needed, turn on Enable Real-time Translation.
Click Join Meeting.
For a recurring meeting, choose the occurrences where Lingo should be scheduled.
This and following meetings: Auto-join this meeting and following occurrences.
All occurrences: Auto-join every occurrence in the recurring event.
This meeting only: Auto-join only the selected meeting.
When setup is complete, Auto join is turned on for the event and the selected languages appear on the card.

chunks.heading: Turn off auto-join
chunks.text:
Turn off Auto join on the event card to stop Lingo from joining that meeting.
If Lingo is scheduled for multiple occurrences in a recurring meeting, choose the removal scope.
All occurrences: Remove Lingo auto-join from the entire recurring event.
This meeting only: Remove Lingo auto-join only from the selected occurrence.

chunks.heading: Connection status problems
chunks.text: If calendar sync fails, an error card for that calendar appears under Upcoming meetings. Select Reconnect on the error card to authorize again. If multiple calendars are connected, only events from the calendar that failed to sync are excluded from the list.

chunks.heading: Considerations
chunks.text: When using Lingo, some features can appear differently depending on the meeting type, browser permissions, and calendar connection status.

chunks.heading: Microphone permission
chunks.text:
To use Microphone or Mic + Screen in an in-person meeting, the browser needs microphone permission.
If microphone permission is denied, Lingo cannot receive audio and cannot start meeting recording. Follow the on-screen guidance to allow microphone permission in the browser or device settings, then try again.

chunks.heading: Screen Audio
chunks.text:
Screen Audio and Mic + Screen are available only when the browser supports screen audio sharing.
When selecting a screen or tab, also select the browser’s audio-sharing option so Lingo can recognize sound played from the screen. If you do not select the audio-sharing option, the screen may be shared but the sound may not be recorded.

chunks.heading: Joining remote meetings
chunks.text:
Remote meetings support Zoom, Google Meet, and MS Teams meeting URLs. If the meeting URL is invalid or unsupported, Lingo may not be able to join the meeting.
If the meeting has a waiting room, the Lingo status can be shown as Awaiting host approval. In this case, the host must admit Lingo before recording and speech recognition can proceed.

chunks.heading: Real-time translation
chunks.text:
To use Enable Real-time Translation, you must first select at least one Source Language. You can select up to three source languages.
When real-time translation is enabled, you can view the original text and translation together during the meeting. If translation is not needed, you can turn it off and keep only the transcript.

chunks.heading: Supported languages
chunks.text:
The same languages can be selected for meetings and Real-time Interpreter.
Korean
Japanese
English
Thai
Vietnamese
Chinese Traditional
BetaEstonian
BetaSpanish
BetaGerman
BetaFrench
BetaPortuguese
BetaItalian
BetaIndonesian

chunks.heading: Real-time Interpreter
chunks.text:
Real-time Interpreter works by holding the microphone button while speaking and releasing it to play translated speech. Keep holding the microphone button while you speak. If the utterance is too short or there is too much background noise, speech may not be detected.
Leaving the Real-time Interpreter screen does not always end an active session immediately. To finish interpretation completely, select End in the top-right corner.
If the organization does not have enough credits when starting Real-time Interpreter, Not enough credit is shown and interpretation cannot start.
See Real-time Interpreter for the full workflow and troubleshooting steps.

chunks.heading: Lingo AI
chunks.text:
Lingo AI generates answers from the meeting transcript. Incomplete recognition or unclear speaker labels can affect its answers, so verify important decisions and dates against the original transcript.
To focus a question on specific content, select and attach the relevant utterances. See Lingo AI for details.

chunks.heading: Calendar events
chunks.text:
The Calendar screen shows only events that have meeting URLs among connected Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook events. Events without meeting links are not shown because Lingo cannot join them.
If calendar authorization expires or sync fails, events from that calendar may not be shown. In this case, select Reconnect from Settings or Calendar to authorize again.

chunks.heading: Public sharing
chunks.text:
When you turn on Public sharing link on the meeting detail screen, anyone with the link can view the shared meeting without signing in.
If needed, set Add password and Link expiration together. A shared link with a password can be opened only by users who know the password, and the link cannot be accessed after the expiration time passes.

chunks.heading: Insufficient credits
chunks.text: If the organization has insufficient credits, you cannot start a meeting or use Real-time Interpreter, AI Summary, or Lingo AI. In this case, Insufficient credits is shown on the screen, and you need to add credits before trying again.

chunks.heading: Custom Keywords
chunks.text: In Custom Keywords, you can register frequently used proper nouns as keywords so Lingo can recognize and translate them more accurately.

chunks.heading: Manage keywords
chunks.text:
Register words that appear often but can be difficult for speech recognition or translation, such as product names, company names, people names, acronyms, and technical terms. Registered keywords are applied to recognition and translation in meetings started afterward.
Keywords are managed in a table. Each row represents one proper noun, and each language column stores the spelling of that proper noun in that language.
For example, entering the Korean, English, and Japanese spellings in the same row helps Lingo recognize them as the same proper noun.

chunks.heading: Add keywords
chunks.text:
Select a cell in an empty row.
Enter the proper noun spelling.
If the same proper noun has spellings in other languages, enter them in the other language columns in the same row.
To add a new proper noun, select Add row at the bottom.
Click a cell to edit it inline. Changes are saved automatically. Saving… is shown while saving, and Auto-saved is shown when saving is complete.

chunks.heading: Manage language columns
chunks.text:
Korean, English, and Japanese columns are shown by default. To register spellings in more languages, select Add language in the top-right corner of the table.
The following languages can be used as language columns.
Korean
Japanese
English
Thai
Vietnamese
Chinese Traditional
Chinese Simplified
Estonian
Spanish
German
French
Portuguese
Italian
Indonesian
Deleting a language column also deletes the terms saved in that language. Before deletion, confirm the language to delete and the number of terms that will be deleted.

chunks.heading: Keyword count and limits
chunks.text:
You can save up to 100 keyword rows.
One row counts as one keyword even if multiple language cells are filled in.
Each cell can contain up to 50 characters.
Empty cells are not saved.
Duplicate terms in the same language column cannot be saved. After you fix the duplicates, auto-save resumes.
The bottom of the screen shows the current number of registered proper nouns and how many more can be added.

chunks.heading: Delete keywords
chunks.text: Select the delete icon on the right side of a row to delete that proper noun. The last empty row cannot be deleted.

chunks.heading: Getting Started
chunks.text:
Lingo is a meeting-recording AIP App that turns meeting audio into text in real time, and lets you continue with translation and AI summaries when needed. For in-person meetings, Lingo records the microphone or screen audio from the current device. For remote meetings, Lingo joins Zoom, Google Meet, or MS Teams meetings and records what people say.
After a meeting ends, the record is saved in Meetings. You can review the meeting, download the transcript, create a public sharing link, or generate an AI summary.
When you access Lingo directly, log in and choose the organization you want to use. When you open Lingo from AIP, you need permission to access Lingo from the Apps menu.

chunks.heading: What you can do with Lingo
chunks.text:
View spoken content as real-time text during a meeting.
View original text and translations together in multilingual meetings.
Use Real-time Interpreter by holding the microphone button, speaking, and playing translated speech right away.
Configure Lingo auto-join for calendar events.
Register frequently used words such as product names, people names, and acronyms as keywords to improve speech recognition accuracy.
Share meeting records or organize them with AI summaries after the meeting ends.

chunks.heading: Basic workflow
chunks.text:
Start an in-person or remote meeting from Home.
Select the Source Language actually used in the meeting.
If translation is needed, turn on Enable Real-time Translation.
For an in-person meeting, click Start Recording to begin recording. For a remote meeting, recording starts when Lingo joins the meeting URL.
When the meeting ends, open Meetings to review the record, share it, download the transcript, or create an AI summary.
When you need to interpret a short conversation right away, select Real-time Interpreter from Home. Hold the microphone button while speaking and release it to play translated speech. After you end the session, the interpretation record is saved in Meetings. See Real-time Interpreter for the full workflow.

chunks.heading: Learn more by menu
chunks.text:
Home: Start a new meeting and check ongoing and scheduled meetings.
Real-time Interpreter: Configure languages and voice, then interpret speech aloud.
Meetings: Open saved meeting records and use sharing, download, delete, and AI summary features.
Lingo AI: Ask questions using a live or ended meeting transcript.
Calendar: Configure Lingo auto-join for Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook events.
Custom Keywords: Register frequently used words as keywords.
Settings: Manage the calendar display window and calendar connection status.
Considerations: Check notes for microphone permissions, screen audio, remote meetings, and public sharing.

chunks.heading: Before first use
chunks.text:
Access Lingo through your organization’s Lingo URL and, if needed, click Login with AIP.
Allow browser microphone permission when using in-person meetings.
Prepare a Zoom, Google Meet, or MS Teams meeting URL when using remote meetings.
Connect Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook before using calendar auto-join.

chunks.heading: Account and organization menu
chunks.text:
In the user area at the bottom of the sidebar, you can check the current organization and signed-in account. Select the user name to open these menus.
Change organization: Move to Lingo for another organization. Use this when you cannot access the current organization or need to check meetings in another organization.
Personal settings: Open the AIP personal settings page. You can check or change language and system settings. After completing settings, you can return to Lingo.
Logout: Sign out of the current account.

chunks.heading: Home
chunks.text: Home is where you start meetings and check the current Lingo status.

chunks.heading: Start of meeting
chunks.text: Choose a meeting type in the Start of meeting area at the top.

chunks.heading: In-Person Meeting
chunks.text:
Record a meeting using audio from the current device.
Item | Description
Audio Source | Choose Microphone, Screen Audio, or Mic + Screen. If the browser does not support screen audio sharing, screen-related options are not shown.
Microphone | When using a microphone, select one of the connected microphones.
Meeting Name | Enter a meeting title. If left blank, the name is created from the current date and time.
Source Language | Select up to three languages actually spoken in the meeting.
Enable Real-time Translation | Shows recognized speech in other selected languages. When enabled, you can view the original text and translated text together on the meeting screen.
Click Create to move to the meeting screen. An in-person meeting starts only after you click Start Recording on the meeting screen.

chunks.heading: Remote Meeting
chunks.text:
Lingo joins a remote meeting URL and records the meeting.
Item | Description
Meeting URL | Enter a Zoom, Google Meet, or MS Teams URL.
Meeting Name | Enter a meeting title. If left blank, the name is created from the current date and time.
Source Language | Select up to three languages actually spoken in the meeting.
Enable Real-time Translation | Shows recognized speech in other selected languages. When enabled, you can view the original text and translated text together on the meeting screen.
Lingo Join Timing | Choose Join Now or Later. If you choose Join Now, Lingo joins the meeting immediately after you click Create. If you choose Later, the meeting is saved as scheduled and can be started later with Lingo Join Now.
If Lingo is waiting before entering a remote meeting and the host has not admitted it yet, the status is shown as Awaiting host approval.

chunks.heading: Real-time Interpreter
chunks.text:
Real-time Interpreter is an interpretation mode where you hold the microphone button while speaking, then release it to hear translated speech right away.
Select the Real-time Interpreter card on Home to open the full-screen interpreter. Configure the languages, output voice, and devices, then hold the microphone button while speaking. See Real-time Interpreter for the full workflow.

chunks.heading: Ongoing meetings
chunks.text:
Ongoing meetings shows meetings that are currently open, recording, or being transcribed. Select a card to move to the meeting screen.
Possible statuses include:
Ongoing: The meeting is in progress.
Paused: Recording is paused.
Real-time Interpreter: An interpretation session is in progress. Select the card to return to the ongoing interpretation screen.
Creating bot…, Bot ready, Bot joining meeting…, Awaiting host approval, Bot in meeting, Recording: Shows the Lingo join status for a remote meeting.
If there are no ongoing meetings, No meeting in progress. is shown.

chunks.heading: Scheduled meetings
chunks.text:
Upcoming scheduled meetings are shown at the bottom of Home. Select a card to move to the meeting screen.
Scheduled meetings show the meeting date and time, meeting name, in-person or remote type, selected languages, and Scheduled meeting or a failure status.
A failure status appears when Lingo could not start the meeting. For example, Insufficient credits appears if the organization does not have enough credits. Start failed or Join Failed can appear when the remote meeting URL has a problem or Lingo could not join the meeting.

chunks.heading: Lingo MCP
chunks.text:
Lingo MCP lets AI access Lingo calendars, meeting sessions, transcripts, summaries, sharing settings, and custom keywords. Combine it with other MCP integrations such as email, calendar, and Salesforce to handle meeting preparation and follow-up in one conversation or automation flow.
Lingo MCP works within the signed-in user’s Lingo permissions and organization scope. Only tools allowed by the organization administrator are available in AIP.

chunks.heading: Before you start
chunks.text:
You must have access to the same organization in QueryPie AIP and Lingo.
The Lingo MCP Integration must be enabled for your organization.

chunks.heading: Connect Lingo MCP to AIP
chunks.text:
Find Lingo MCP in QueryPie AIP’s MCP menu or in an Agent’s tool list.
Select Install and review the tool list. When using Lingo MCP in an Agent, select the tools the Agent needs.
To use it with other services, add calendar, email, Salesforce, or other MCP tools to the same Agent.
Select that Agent in AIP Chat.
For more information about installing MCP integrations, configuring Agent tools, and using AIP Chat, see QueryPie AIP Quickstart.

chunks.heading: User and calendar
chunks.text:
Tool | Description
lingo_whoami | Returns the currently signed-in Lingo user and organization.
lingo_list_calendar_accounts | Lists calendar accounts connected to Lingo and their status, including expired tokens or reconnection requirements.
lingo_list_calendar_events | Lists events from connected calendars and shows the interpreter bot reservation status for each event.
lingo_sync_calendar | Imports the latest events from the calendar provider into Lingo. Use it when a new, moved, or missing event does not appear.

chunks.heading: Interpreter bot and sessions
chunks.text:
Tool | Description
lingo_schedule_meeting_bot | Schedules the Lingo interpreter bot for a calendar event. Translation languages are required so the bot can record and translate the meeting.
lingo_cancel_meeting_bot | Removes a scheduled interpreter bot before the meeting starts.
lingo_create_session | Creates an in-person or remote session without a calendar event. Choose translation or transcription mode and optionally have the bot join immediately.
lingo_get_session | Returns a session’s title, start and end time, status, meeting type, mode, and meeting URL.
lingo_search_sessions | Searches sessions by title, date range, status, and meeting type, including sessions in progress.
lingo_update_session | Changes a session title or adds translation languages. Languages can only be added before the session starts.

chunks.heading: Meeting results and sharing
chunks.text:
Tool | Description
lingo_get_transcript | Reads a session transcript in chronological order, either in the original language or a selected translation language.
lingo_generate_summary | Generates a new summary for a completed session. You can specify the summary focus. This consumes organization credits.
lingo_get_summary | Reads a summary already stored for the session without writing data or consuming credits.
lingo_get_session_sharing | Checks whether a session is shared externally and returns its link, password, expiration date, and other sharing details.

chunks.heading: Custom keywords
chunks.text:
Tool | Description
lingo_get_hotwords | Lists the current user’s personal custom keywords.
lingo_add_hotword | Adds a proper noun or domain term and its spelling for each language.
lingo_update_hotword | Changes language-specific spellings for an existing custom keyword.

chunks.heading: Use case 1: Schedule a meeting and email the participants
chunks.text:
Use calendar and email MCP tools together with Lingo MCP to find or create an event, schedule the interpreter bot, and send the sharing link to participants.
Create a meeting or find an existing event with a calendar MCP.
Run lingo_sync_calendar to bring the latest event into Lingo.
Use lingo_list_calendar_events to confirm the event and its bot reservation status.
Schedule the bot and select translation languages with lingo_schedule_meeting_bot.
When the session is ready, use lingo_get_session_sharing to verify the sharing link and access requirements.
Send an email containing the schedule, languages, and sharing link with an email MCP.
Example request:
Find next Tuesday’s customer meeting and schedule the Lingo interpreter bot for Korean and English. When the sharing link is ready, draft an email with the meeting time and link for the participants. Show me the recipients and message for approval before sending.
If the sharing link has a password or expiration date, include the required access information. Verify recipients and the intended sharing scope before sending the link outside your organization.

chunks.heading: Use case 2: Send a meeting summary to Salesforce
chunks.text:
After a meeting ends, retrieve or generate a Lingo summary and add it to the relevant customer or opportunity record in Salesforce.
Find the completed customer meeting with lingo_search_sessions.
Check for an existing summary with lingo_get_summary.
If no summary exists or a different format is required, use lingo_generate_summary with a sales-focused instruction.
Use Salesforce MCP to find the related Account, Opportunity, or activity record.
Show the target record and proposed update to the user for confirmation.
After approval, write the summary, customer requirements, decisions, and next steps to Salesforce.
Example request:
Find today’s completed meeting with ABC and read its saved summary. If it has no summary, generate one focused on customer requirements, objections, decisions, and next steps. Find the related Salesforce Opportunity, show me the proposed update, and write it only after I approve.

chunks.heading: More ways to use Lingo MCP
chunks.text:
Prepare terminology: Add customer and product names with lingo_add_hotword before the meeting.
Check a live meeting: Find an active session with lingo_search_sessions and read the discussion so far with lingo_get_transcript.
Create follow-up tasks: Extract action items by owner from the transcript or summary and add them to a project management tool.
Audit sharing: Check externally shared sessions and review link passwords and expiration dates.

chunks.heading: Use Lingo MCP safely
chunks.text:
Review targets and content before actions that affect external systems, such as scheduling, sending email, or updating Salesforce.
Transcripts, summaries, and sharing links may contain sensitive meeting information. Use them within your organization’s policy and participant consent.
If a tool is unavailable, check the organization’s MCP activation status, tool access policy, and the organization selected in Lingo.

chunks.heading: Meetings
chunks.text: Meetings shows scheduled meetings and saved meeting records.

chunks.heading: Scheduled meetings
chunks.text:
Scheduled meetings at the top shows meetings that have not started yet.
Each card shows:
Meeting date and time
Meeting name
In-person or remote meeting icon
Selected languages
Scheduled meeting or a start failure status
Remote meeting platform: Google Meet, Zoom, or MS Teams
Lingo join status for the remote meeting
Select a card to move to the meeting screen. If a remote meeting has not started yet, you can click Lingo Join Now on the meeting screen to let Lingo join the meeting.
In the more menu on the right side of the card, you can use Share and Delete. When deleting a recurring meeting, This meeting only and All occurrences are shown so you can choose whether to delete only this occurrence or remove the Lingo schedule from the entire recurring event.

chunks.heading: All meetings
chunks.text:
All meetings shows meeting records that are completed or in progress. More items load as you scroll down.
Each card shows:
Meeting date and time
Meeting name
In-person or remote meeting icon
Selected languages
Status such as Ongoing, Paused, Cancelled, Join Failed, or Shared
Lingo join status for the remote meeting
Select a card to open the meeting detail screen. Meetings that have not ended yet can be opened again in the meeting screen.
In the more menu on the right side of the card, you can use Share, Download transcript, and Delete. If a remote meeting is still in progress and Lingo is in the meeting, Remove Bot is shown. Selecting it removes Lingo from the meeting and ends that remote meeting record.
Select Live interpretation in the meeting type filter to view only Real-time Interpreter sessions. A Real-time Interpreter record stores what the user said while holding the microphone and the translated result.

chunks.heading: Meeting detail
chunks.text:
On the meeting detail screen, you can review saved text and translations.
Available actions include:
Select the meeting name: Edit the name.
Share: Create and configure a public sharing link.
Download transcript: Download the meeting transcript as a TXT file.
Delete: Delete the meeting.
AI Summary: Summarize an ended meeting.
Lingo AI: Ask questions and review answers based on the meeting transcript.
Language filter: Show All languages or only a specific language.

chunks.heading: Lingo AI
chunks.text:
Select the Lingo AI face icon button on the right side of the meeting screen to open the panel and ask questions about the full transcript or selected utterances. It is available in live and ended meetings and supports suggested and free-form questions.
See Lingo AI to learn how to attach utterances and manage the chat.

chunks.heading: AI Summary
chunks.text:
Select AI Summary on the meeting detail screen to use these templates.
Default Summary: Summarizes key points, decisions, and next actions.
Action Items: Organizes tasks by assignee, deadlines, and follow-ups.
Meeting Minutes: Organizes discussion and outcomes by agenda item in a meeting-minutes format.
Key Decisions: Organizes decisions with their background and rationale.
If you want a different format, enter it in Custom Prompt and click Generate. You can copy the generated summary with Copy summary.

chunks.heading: Public sharing
chunks.text:
Select Share on the meeting detail screen and turn on Public sharing link to create a sharing link. Anyone with the link can view the shared meeting without signing in.
Sharing settings include:
Copy Link: Copy the sharing link.
QR code: Scan to open the sharing link.
Link expiration: Set the sharing link expiration date and time, or leave it as Never.
Add password: Add a password to the sharing link.
Unshare: Turn off public sharing.
Opening a sharing link displays the Shared session screen. On the shared session screen, viewers can review the meeting and use these actions.
Share link: Copy the current shared session link again or share it as a QR code.
Presentation mode: Shows the transcribed and translated text in a near full-screen view.
Download transcript: Download the shared meeting transcript as a TXT file.
When a viewer opens a password-protected sharing link, Share link lets them choose Copy with password or Copy link only. Users without password access information must enter the password to open the shared session.

chunks.heading: Presentation mode
chunks.text:
Presentation mode focuses entirely on the transcribed and translated text, removing all other UI elements. It is ideal for situations such as presentations or real-time interpretation, where participants only need to see the live transcription or translation.
To enter presentation mode, select the presentation icon in the meeting screen header. It opens in a new browser tab. To exit, close the tab.

chunks.heading: Display options
chunks.text:
Select the settings button in the top-right corner to adjust display options.
Option | Description
Mode | Choose what to display: Both (source and translation side by side), Source only, or Translation only.
Text size | Adjust the transcript text size across five steps.
Alignment | Set the text alignment to Left or Center.
Theme | Switch between Light and Dark themes.
Emphasize current | Highlight the most recent utterance to make it easier to follow.
Your display preferences are saved and restored the next time you open presentation mode.

chunks.heading: Lingo Voice (Real-time Interpreter)
chunks.text: Lingo Voice is a real-time interpreting feature that translates speech between supported languages and plays the result aloud. For example, Korean speech can be translated and played in Japanese. Users can select the input language, output language, and output voice for multilingual presentations and in-person communication. Real-time Interpreter is a Beta feature and uses the organization's AIP credits.

chunks.heading: Real-time Interpreter
chunks.text:
Real-time Interpreter recognizes speech while you hold the microphone button, then translates and plays it aloud in the selected language when you release the button. It is designed for short conversations and turn-by-turn, in-person communication.
Real-time Interpreter is a Beta feature and uses your organization’s AIP credits.

chunks.heading: Start Real-time Interpreter
chunks.text:
In the meeting start area on Home, select Real-time Interpreter.
If the browser asks for microphone access, select Allow.
Check Your language, Their language, the output voice, and the microphone at the top of the screen.
Hold the microphone button while speaking.
Release the button when you finish.
The translated sentence appears on screen and plays aloud in the other language.
If you have used Real-time Interpreter before, Lingo restores your last language pair and output voice.

chunks.heading: Interpret a conversation
chunks.text:
Each utterance moves through the following states.
State | Description
Connecting… | Lingo is preparing the connection and microphone.
Hold to speak | The interpreter is ready. Hold the microphone button and speak.
Listening | Lingo is receiving your speech. Keep holding the button until you finish.
Translating… | Lingo is transcribing and translating your speech.
Playing… | Lingo displays the translation and plays it with the selected voice.
While Lingo is translating or playing audio, select Cancel to stop the current turn and return to the ready state. You can also hold the microphone button during playback to interrupt it and begin a new utterance.
Lingo may not detect speech if you release the button too quickly or if the environment is noisy. If Didn’t catch that appears, hold the button longer, speak clearly, and select Try again.

chunks.heading: Configure languages, voice, and devices
chunks.text:
The top of the interpreter shows the current language pair, output voice, and microphone. Select the swap button between the languages to exchange Your language and Their language immediately.
Select Edit to change the settings during an interpretation session.
Setting | Description
Your language | Select the language you will speak.
Their language | Select the language for the translated text and audio. It cannot be the same as Your language.
Swap languages | Exchange Your language and Their language.
Output voice | Select the voice used to play translations. You can preview voices that include a play button.
Microphone & output | Select the microphone and output device. When microphone access is allowed, you can also check the input level.
Select Done to apply your changes. If you select Cancel or close the dialog, Lingo keeps the previous settings.
See Supported languages under Considerations for the available languages.

chunks.heading: End or leave an interpretation
chunks.text:
To finish the session, select End in the upper-right corner. Lingo saves the completed interpretation under Meetings.
If you only use the back button, the session remains available temporarily instead of ending immediately. When you select Real-time Interpreter again from Home, choose one of the following:
Continue: Return to the ongoing interpretation.
Start new: End the existing interpretation and start another one.
Cancel: Close the prompt and stay on Home.

chunks.heading: Review interpretation records
chunks.text:
Completed interpretations are saved in the all meetings list under Meetings. Select Real-time Interpreter in the meeting type filter to show only interpretation records.
From an interpretation detail page, you can:
Review the source and translation for each utterance
Create a public sharing link
Download the audio record
Delete the record

chunks.heading: Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
Situation | What to check
Microphone access is blocked | Allow microphone access for Lingo in the browser or device settings, then reconnect the microphone.
Didn’t catch that appears | Hold the button longer and speak clearly near the microphone.
The connection is lost | Check your network, end the interpreter screen, and start again.
Credits are insufficient | Add organization credits in AIP and try again.

chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text: In Settings, you manage the upcoming meeting period shown on the Calendar screen and the calendar connection status.

chunks.heading: Calendar Window
chunks.text:
Calendar Window determines how many days of upcoming schedules are shown in Upcoming meetings on the Calendar screen.
Available values are:
1 day
3 days
5 days
7 days (default)
14 days
21 days
28 days
When you change the value, it is saved immediately without a separate save button. After that, the Calendar screen shows only events within the selected period that have meeting URLs.

chunks.heading: Calendar
chunks.text:
In the Calendar section, you connect or disconnect Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook accounts.
Supported calendars are:
Google Calendar
Microsoft Outlook
Each calendar item shows information and buttons depending on its current status.
Status | Display
Not connected | Connect
Connected | Connected email address and Disconnect
Authorization expired or sync failed | Error message and Reconnect
Connection in progress | Setting up…

chunks.heading: Connect calendar
chunks.text: Select Connect for the calendar you want to connect. You are moved to the account authorization screen for that calendar. After authorization is completed, Lingo syncs calendar events, and events with meeting URLs appear in Upcoming meetings on the Calendar screen.

chunks.heading: Reconnect calendar
chunks.text: If calendar authorization expires or sync fails, the item shows an error message and Reconnect. Select Reconnect and authorize again to restore event sync.

chunks.heading: Disconnect calendar
chunks.text: Select Disconnect on a connected calendar to disconnect it from Lingo. After disconnecting, upcoming meetings from that calendar no longer appear on the Calendar screen.

chunks.heading: 🌟 What is QueryPie AIP?
chunks.text:
QueryPie AIP(AI Platform) is an AI Playground where you can combine MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to create various agents and run them instantly.
You can use various SaaS applications such as Slack, JIRA, Discord, as well as workflow tools like n8n and Dify through MCP.

chunks.heading: 🚀 Easy MCP Server Integration
chunks.text:
We provide carefully selected MCP servers that can be immediately applied to your work.
AWS
n8n
Dify
Slack
Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Sheets, etc.
Jira, Confluence
We also provide various other MCP servers. Check out the Available MCP Servers documentation.

chunks.heading: 🔧 MCP Preset Management
chunks.text: You can save frequently used MCP servers and Instructions as presets.

chunks.heading: 💬 LLM Chat
chunks.text:
You can start chatting by mentioning presets.
Currently supports various latest models such as Claude Opus 4.7, OpenAI GPT-5.5, Google Gemini 3.5 Flash, etc.
By following the 🚀 Quickstart documentation, you can integrate frequently used business applications in just a few minutes.
For frequently asked questions, check the FAQ documentation.

chunks.heading: 🛠️ Supported LLM Apps
chunks.text:
QueryPie AIP supports various LLM applications.
By running the local proxy installation commands provided for each MCP preset, you can install them in your desired LLM application.

chunks.heading: Supported LLM Applications
chunks.text:
Cursor
Claude Desktop
Windsurf
Devin

chunks.heading: How to Use in Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf
chunks.text:
Select an MCP preset.
Click the Generate Command button in the Installation tab.
The generated local proxy installation command is valid for 10 minutes and can only be used once.
Open a terminal and run the local proxy installation command.
Once the local proxy installation is complete, you can use QueryPie AIP’s MCP presets in your LLM application.

chunks.heading: How to Use in Devin
chunks.text:
Select an MCP preset.
Click the Generate Command button in the Installation tab.
Access Devin.
Go to Devin > Settings > Organization Settings > MCP Marketplace.
Select Add Your Own to add an MCP.
Choose STDIO as the Transport Type.
Enter the Command and Arguments generated in step 2 into the STDIO Configuration Command and Arguments fields as shown in the example below.
Click Save changes to add the new MCP.

chunks.heading: Important Notes
chunks.text:
Installation commands for Cursor, Claude Desktop, and Windsurf are valid for 10 minutes and can only be used once.
The CLI Token used for actual authentication is stored in the MCP Configuration. Be careful not to expose the CLI Token.
Issued CLI Tokens can be deleted in Profile > Settings > CLI Token menu.
MCP Preset Instructions do not work in 3rd Party LLM applications.
The maximum number of tools that can be integrated depends on the constraints of the LLM application.
Cursor: 40 tools
Claude Desktop: 10 tools
Windsurf: 100 tools

chunks.heading: Agent Usage Guide
chunks.text:
This guide explains how to automate work and improve efficiency using agents provided by AIP.
Agents are divided into organization agents and personal agents.
Organization agents: Agents created by administrators and shared with organization users.
Personal agents: Agents that users create and configure for their own work style.

chunks.heading: Common Features
chunks.text:
View and select available agents
Automate work through chat with agents
View agent details
Perform tasks using MCP Integrations and Skills
View agent execution history and results

chunks.heading: Viewing the Agent List
chunks.text:
Click Agents in the left menu to view the agents you can use.
On the Agents screen, the following tabs may be available depending on agent type.
Personal Agents: Agents that you created yourself
Organization Agents: Agents shared by the organization

chunks.heading: Agent Chat Features
chunks.text:
You can visually check context window usage at the bottom right of the chat input field. This helps you identify when to start a new conversation before the agent’s space for processing conversation context becomes full and response quality degrades.
While the agent is generating a response, progress status text and elapsed time are displayed together, so you can intuitively understand the response process.
The footer of each agent response shows the credits used for that response.
When tools are called, the MCP Integration name, Tool name, and Skill name are displayed together, so you can clearly see which source the agent is using to perform the task.
Agents automatically provide a Built-in Skill for document file processing (PDF, Excel, PPTX, DOCX analysis). Uploaded documents can be analyzed quickly and accurately without additional setup. Files are supported up to 200 MB per turn. There is no cumulative limit per session.
AI Image Generation: Agents connected to an image generation MCP can generate images directly from text prompts. Describe the image you want in the chat, and the agent generates it so you can view it directly in the conversation.
Web app and widget creation: In agent chat, you can ask the agent to create a Web app or data visualization widget. Conversation results can be turned into executable forms such as business dashboards, search screens, or simple internal tools.
TTS responses: You can listen to agent responses by voice. The voice follows the TTS voice setting in User Settings.

chunks.heading: Agent Chat Features
chunks.text:
Dedicated chat-only links: You can use links that open the chat screen for a specific agent directly. Users who receive the link can talk to that agent without going through the agent settings screen.
Start agents from the launcher screen: Launcher role users can see assigned agents as tiles and start a new chat immediately by selecting the agent they want to use.

chunks.heading: Organization Agents
chunks.text: Organization agents are agents created by administrators and shared with organization users. Users can select and use agents shared by the organization.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
Organization administrators configure the agent’s purpose, description, Instruction, Integrations, and Skills.
Users can select a shared organization agent to start a chat.
If the administrator configured “Require User Authentication”, users must enter authentication information themselves.

chunks.heading: Organization Agent Details
chunks.text:
On the organization agent detail screen, you can view the following information.
Overview tab:
Detailed description of the agent’s functionality
Information about services that can be connected
Configuration tab:
Service integration settings that require user authentication
Suppress personal memory setting
Security tab:
For agents where an administrator has allowed external service connection, you can check the A2A Endpoint and Agent Card URL.
In Manage Access Token, you can issue, copy, and revoke the A2A Access Token used by external services to call the agent.
Register the Agent Card URL or Endpoint and Access Token in the external service to call the agent from that service.
Suppress Personal Memory:
If you turn on the Suppress Personal Memory toggle at the bottom of the Configuration tab, the agent will not save the user’s personal memory or use it in future conversations.
If the administrator disabled personal memory at the agent level, a Locked by Admin badge is displayed and users cannot change the setting themselves.
Dedicated chat-only link:
If a dedicated link is provided for an agent shared by the organization, users can start chatting with that specific agent directly through the link.
Link access permissions can be configured together.
This is useful for workflows such as customer support, internal FAQs, and approval requests where users should be routed directly to a specific agent.

chunks.heading: Starting an Agent from the Launcher Screen
chunks.text:
When you access an organization with the Launcher role, the New Chat screen displays only the agents you can use instead of the general chat list or agent settings screen. Select an agent from this screen to start chatting immediately.
How to use:
Log in with an account assigned the Launcher role.
When you enter the organization, check the accessible agent tiles on the New Chat screen.
Review the name and summary on the agent tile you want to use.
Click Start chat to move to a new chat with that agent.
Information shown on the screen:
Agent icon
Agent name
Agent summary
Start chat button
If there are no accessible agents, No agents assigned is displayed. In this case, ask the organization administrator to assign an agent you can use.

chunks.heading: Personal Agents
chunks.text:
Personal agents are agents that users create and configure themselves. You can configure the model, instructions, Skills, and Integrations for your personal work style and use the agent directly in chat.
The feature previously provided as Preset is planned to transition to personal agents. Existing Presets can be migrated to personal agents by using the Import from Preset button. Because the Preset feature will be phased out over time, we recommend configuring new work based on personal agents.

chunks.heading: Key Features
chunks.text:
Users can create and delete personal agents themselves.
Users can import a personal agent based on an existing Preset.
Users can configure the agent name, description, and icon, and can generate an icon based on the name and summary.
Users can write the agent description and example prompts themselves.
Users can configure the LLM model, Instruction, Skills, Integrations, and generation options themselves.

chunks.heading: Creating a Personal Agent
chunks.text:
In the Personal Agents tab, click the New Agent button to create a personal agent.
Basic information:
Name: Enter the personal agent name.
Summary: Enter a short description to display in the list.
Icon: Upload an icon to distinguish the agent, or click Generate icon to create an icon that matches the name and Summary. Credits are used when generating icons.
After creation is complete, you can configure additional settings on the personal agent detail screen.

chunks.heading: Import from Preset
chunks.text:
Use the Import from Preset button to create a personal agent based on an existing Preset.
After you select the Preset to import, a personal agent is created based on the settings included in that Preset. Some Integrations may require re-authentication after import.

chunks.heading: Personal Agent Details
chunks.text:
On the personal agent detail screen, use the Overview and Configuration tabs to manage how the agent works.
Overview tab:
Description: Describe the agent’s role and how to use it.
Example prompts: Register example questions that users can refer to when starting with the agent.
Configuration tab:
LLM Model: Select the model the agent will use.
Instruction: Write the instructions the agent should follow.
Skills: Select the Skills the agent will use.
Integrations: Connect MCP Integrations the agent will use.
Generation options: Configure file upload support, Artifacts usage, maximum output tokens, and whether to save personal memory.
Use Web apps, widgets, and TTS: You can ask the agent to create Web apps or widgets and provide responses by voice.

chunks.heading: Important Notes
chunks.text:
Authentication information management: Safely manage information for services that require personal authentication.
Permission verification: Regularly review the permissions for data and services that the agent can access.
Skill changes: If you modify a Skill, start a new chat so the changes are applied reliably.
Sensitive information protection: Handle requests that contain personal or confidential information carefully.
A2A Access Token management: Keep tokens used for external service connection secure, and revoke tokens you no longer use.

chunks.heading: 📦 AIP Apps
chunks.text:
AIP Apps are apps that connect directly to QueryPie AIP and extend what you can do in your AI workspace.
Below are the currently available AIP Apps.
Currently, AIP Apps are available only to AIP partners. If you want to become a partner, please contact us through Contact Us .

chunks.heading: Lingo
chunks.text: Transcribe meeting speech in real time and translate across Korean, English, and Japanese simultaneously.

chunks.heading: NotePie
chunks.text: Turn documents, URLs, and text into study guides, mind maps, slide decks, podcasts, and cited AI chat.

chunks.heading: LinkPie
chunks.text: Manage business-card contacts and coordinate meetings with contact search, OCR, scheduling, and follow-up workflows.

chunks.heading: Automation
chunks.text:
Automation allows you to automatically run agents based on specific triggers, such as a scheduled time or receiving an email.
QueryPie AI’s Automation feature allows you to automate repetitive tasks to streamline your workflow. You can set it to periodically run an Agent at a specific time or trigger it to perform desired actions when an email meeting certain conditions is received.

chunks.heading: Automation Menu
chunks.text: In the Automation menu, you can see a list of created automations at a glance.

chunks.heading: Creating and Editing Automation
chunks.text: You can create a new Automation or change existing settings.

chunks.heading: Select Trigger Type
chunks.text:
Select how to execute the automation.
Schedule Trigger: Executes the automation at a specified time or interval.
Email Trigger: Executes the automation when an email meeting certain conditions is received.
Webhook Trigger: Executes the automation when an event occurs in external systems such as Salesforce, GitHub, or Jira. You can trigger automation from any external system via a custom Webhook URL.
Folder Watch Trigger: Automatically executes the automation when file changes occur in a specific folder in My Drive, Google Drive, or Box.

chunks.heading: 1. Schedule Trigger Settings
chunks.text:
If you select ‘Schedule Trigger’ as the Trigger Type, you can automate repetitive tasks at a specified time or interval.
Schedule Name: Specify a unique name to identify the schedule.
Selected Agent: Select the agent to execute automatically.
Prompt: Write the command or request to pass to the agent when the schedule runs.
One Time: A one-time schedule that runs only once.
Custom: Repeatedly runs every minute within the user-specified days of the week and time range.
Daily: Repeatedly runs at a specified time every day.
Weekly: Repeatedly runs at a specific day and time.
Monthly: Repeatedly runs on a monthly basis.
Specify the desired date and time exactly.
Ensure accurate execution timing through time zone settings.

chunks.heading: 2. Email Trigger Settings
chunks.text:
If you select ‘Email Trigger’ as the Trigger Type, the following settings are required.
Email Provider: You can choose between Gmail or Outlook.
OAuth Integration: Integrate the selected email account to grant permission to check new emails and execute triggers.
To prevent unnecessary trigger executions, set filters so that automation runs only for emails that meet specific conditions. Properly setting filters can reduce unnecessary executions and costs.
Note: Emails sent to yourself will not activate the trigger.
Filter by Labels/Folders (Required): Select the mailbox to check for email triggers.
Gmail: Select Label (Sent, Draft labels are not supported)
Outlook: Select Folder (Sent Items, Drafts folders are not supported)
Filter Events (Optional): Set specific conditions to ensure automation runs only for desired emails.
Conditions Match Type:
Match All conditions (AND): Executes when all conditions are met.
Match Any condition (OR): Executes when any of the conditions are met.
Condition:
Property: Select from From, Cc, Subject, Bcc.
Operator: Select from Contains, Equals, Is not empty.
Value: Enter the text corresponding to the condition.

chunks.heading: 3. Webhook Trigger Settings
chunks.text:
If you select ‘Webhook Trigger’ as the Trigger Type, you can receive events from external systems to execute agents.
Webhook Name: Specify a name to identify the webhook.
Selected Agent: Select the agent to execute.
Prompt: Write the prompt to pass to the agent. You can utilize the data (Payload) delivered via the webhook in the prompt.
Additional settings may be required depending on the selected Provider.
Salesforce:
Salesforce Organization ID: Enter the ID of the Salesforce organization to integrate.
GitHub / Jira:
Webhook secret: Enter the Webhook Secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification.
Custom:
Selecting Custom as the Provider issues a general-purpose Webhook URL not tied to any specific service. Any external service capable of sending HTTP POST requests—such as Slack, Teams, or internal systems—can call this URL to trigger Automation.
Secret (optional): Set an arbitrary secret value for request verification. When set, the X-Webhook-Secret value in the request header must match.
After creating an Automation, you can check and manage the Webhook URL on the detail screen.
Check and Copy URL: Copy the generated unique Webhook URL and register it in the webhook settings of external systems.
Regenerate URL: If you need to change the URL for security reasons, you can use the Regenerate URL feature to issue a new URL.

chunks.heading: 4. Folder Watch Trigger Settings
chunks.text:
If you select ‘Folder Watch Trigger’ as the Trigger Type, you can automatically execute an agent when file changes occur in a specific folder in My Drive, Google Drive, or Box.
Automation Name: Specify a name to identify the automation.
Selected Agent: Select the agent to execute automatically when a file is uploaded.
Prompt: Write the command to pass to the agent. The uploaded file’s metadata (filename, size, format, etc.) and file contents are automatically passed to the agent, allowing the agent to directly read and process the file.
Folder to Watch: Select the My Drive or Google Drive folder to monitor.
Files to Watch: Select the file types to monitor. Multiple categories can be selected, and custom extensions can be added manually.
All files: Monitor all files.
Documents: Monitor document files. (pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, doc, xls, ppt)
Images: Monitor image files. (jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp)
Text/Data: Monitor text and data files. (csv, tsv, txt, md, json, xml)
Add custom extensions: Add extensions not included in the above categories manually. (e.g., epub, zip)
Note: Folder Watch Trigger only detects file upload (creation) events. File modifications, deletions, and moves do not trigger the automation.
Note: Folder Watch Trigger supports My Drive, Google Drive, and Box.
Note: When multiple files are uploaded simultaneously, the agent is executed individually for each file.
Note: Folder Watch Trigger operates on an event-based model only, so the Run Now feature is not available.

chunks.heading: Automation Detail Screen and Management
chunks.text:
You can efficiently manage created Automations.
Notification Settings: You can individually toggle notifications on/off for each Automation. Turn off notifications if you only want the automation to process in the background, and turn them on when you want to check execution results. Notifications can be viewed in the Notification Center.
Status Management: You can change the status between Active (running normally) and Paused (temporarily suspended).
Run Now: You can execute immediately without waiting for the scheduled time using the Run Now feature.
Cancel Execution: When an Automation is in the ‘Running’ status, you can immediately stop the task via the Cancel running schedule icon.
If the Trigger is Email or Webhook, the Run Now button is not displayed, and the configured filter information is shown.

chunks.heading: Check Execution History
chunks.text:
You can check the execution results of Automations in detail.
Execution Results: You can check the status as Success, Failure, or Canceled, along with detailed results.
Chat History: A new chat room is created for each execution, and you can check the detailed conversation content by clicking the chat icon. The chat history is maintained even if the agent is deleted.

chunks.heading: Chat
chunks.text: Through chat, you can converse with various LLM models and utilize tools to automate your work.

chunks.text:

You can select different models for each browser tab, allowing you to compare multiple models simultaneously or use them for different purposes.
You can also start a conversation by calling a preset by pressing the @ button in the input field at the bottom of the screen.

chunks.text:
Japan region-based model options are available to help meet data processing location and compliance requirements in Japanese enterprise environments.
